title: 2d6
synopsis: A short RPG-design zine examining how much information can be drawn from a single 2d6 roll beyond simply adding the dice. It explores probability curves, doubles, individual die values, subtraction, ordering, and other interpretations, offering examples of how designers can turn familiar dice into richer resolution mechanics.

title: A Land Once Magic
synopsis: A conversational worldbuilding game for two or more players that creates a distinctive fantasy setting through prompts and discussion. Players establish a shared palette, invent forms of magic, and explore their consequences from different perspectives, either building a new world from scratch or adding depth to one that already exists.

title: A Torch in the Dark
synopsis: A solo dungeon-delving RPG about entering dangerous ruins, reclaiming wealth from undead nobles, and surviving long enough to try again. Cards generate encounters while six-sided dice resolve risks; successful expeditions alternate with downtime spent recovering, resupplying, and preparing for the next descent into the dark.

title: Advanced Fantasy Dungeons
synopsis: A procedural fantasy adventure game built around classic ability scores, distinct character classes, and rulings made between players and a referee. Its rules cover journeys, dungeon exploration, hazards, hirelings, downtime, combat, magic, and domain-level play, providing a broad framework for campaigns driven by dangerous expeditions and player choices.

title: Against Time and Death
synopsis: An asynchronous duet storytelling game about elite operatives serving opposing factions in a multiversal time war. The players create the conflict and their rival agents, then alternate framing scenes across time and space, communicating indirectly through schemes and secret letters before an eight-scene struggle reaches its final reckoning.

title: Agon
synopsis: A mythic adventure RPG about larger-than-life heroes voyaging through a strange, mist-shrouded sea on their journey home. One Strife Player presents islands and trials while the other players seek divine favour, overcome dangers, compete for Glory, and forge legends inspired by the passions and tragedies of Greek epic.

title: Alice is Missing
synopsis: A silent, GMless roleplaying game about the disappearance of teenager Alice Briarwood from the small town of Silent Falls. Over a tightly timed session, players create characters and relationships, then communicate entirely through phone messages while cards introduce suspects, locations, and clues that gradually reveal what happened to Alice.

title: Alone on a Journey
synopsis: A collection of three reflective solo journaling games about solitary exploration: travelling between strange planets, wandering an ancient city, and discovering unsettling objects in a shifting forest. Each uses a six-sided die and playing cards to generate discoveries, inviting the player to record brief impressions and connect them into a personal journey.

title: Apocalypse Frame
synopsis: A fast, mission-focused mech RPG set after an alien Infection transformed a world already collapsing into crisis. Players create elite Aces and customise powerful Frames, then deploy against hostile factions and altered wildlife in tactical, ability-driven combat using the streamlined LUMEN system, with rules for recruitment, advancement, and non-combat operations.

title: Apocalypse World
synopsis: A landmark post-apocalyptic RPG about volatile people trying to survive amid scarcity, danger, and broken communities. Character playbooks and fiction-triggered moves drive action, while the Master of Ceremonies follows principles, threats, and fronts to make the world feel real, put relationships under pressure, and discover what happens through play.

title: Astroprisma Early Access
synopsis: A solo retrofuturist science-fiction roleplaying game about exploring a post-apocalyptic galaxy after the fall of great interstellar empires. Procedural hexcrawls generate planets, ruins, encounters, factions, quests, and difficult bosses, while character origins, equipment, hacking, cybertechnology, and alliances let each spacefarer shape the fate of the systems they discover.

title: Augmented Reality
synopsis: A system-neutral toolkit for improvising dense cyberpunk cities with minimal preparation. Its extensive random tables generate neighbourhood details, street activity, businesses, missions, motivations, and more than 250 varied NPCs, helping a Gamesmaster rapidly add futuristic texture and complications to any dark metropolitan setting without interrupting the action.

title: Avi Maria
synopsis: A solo journaling RPG of robot-girl radicalisation inspired by Metropolis. You play Maria, an apparently ordinary woman drawn back to a hidden laboratory containing an archive of society's failures and a mechanical double that looks exactly like her, using prompts and 2d6 as repeated experiments transform her body and beliefs.

title: Barkeep on the Borderlands
synopsis: A system-neutral pubcrawl pointcrawl adventure set around the drinking establishments of a fantasy border keep. The party races through a night of taverns, rumours, rivalries, setbacks, and unusual drinks, using portable procedures for intoxication and time while pursuing an urgent objective before the evening runs out.

title: Basic Witches
synopsis: A one-page paranormal RPG about teenage femmes using witchcraft to survive school, confront predators, ace exams, and challenge a local Big Bad. Characters combine familiar high-school roles with distinctive magical powers, resolving uncertain actions with a simple d6 system while embracing friendship, feminism, sexuality, and gleefully mundane spellcasting.

title: Beam Saber
synopsis: A Forged in the Dark military-mecha RPG about pilots and their squad fighting missions within a larger, shifting war. Play follows both the machines and the people inside them through tactical operations, stress, relationships, rival factions, and campaign-scale consequences, with extensive options for pilot playbooks, vehicles, squads, and political conflict.

title: Blades in the Dark
synopsis: A crew-focused fantasy crime RPG about daring scoundrels building an underworld enterprise in the haunted industrial city of Doskvol. Play revolves around scores, faction conflicts, consequences, downtime, and the ambitions and vices of both characters and crew, with mechanics designed to move quickly past planning and into risky action.

title: Blades in the Dark Doskvol Breathes
cover: covers/ttrpg/Blades in the Dark Doskvol Breathes.jpg
synopsis: An unofficial Blades in the Dark downtime expansion built around ten short vignettes that give the crew space to inhabit Doskvol beyond scores and recovery rolls. Players replace downtime actions with small, character-focused scenes, asking questions and exploring ordinary places and relationships before retiring the supplement after eight different vignettes.

title: Blades in the Dark Steelweaver’s Rebellion
cover: covers/ttrpg/Blades in the Dark Steelweaver’s Rebellion.jpg
synopsis: An unofficial Blades in the Dark campaign module about working-class resistance in Coalridge. It provides a community under pressure, competing factions, characters, locations, and opportunities for a crew to support an organised rebellion, shifting the game's criminal-action framework toward solidarity, political struggle, and fighting alongside the people who live there.

title: Blood Fish Isle
synopsis: A compact, system-neutral fantasy island adventure centred on the halfling fishing village of Blud Dal'r and the ominous ruins of Srav Hall. A hex map, terse locations, random encounters, dangerous magic, undead threats, and the monstrous Blood Fish give a referee the material needed for an open-ended expedition.

title: Blood Lock
synopsis: A prompt-driven vampire-punk storytelling game about a tense web connecting a hungry Vampire, captive Victim, devoted Thrall, and relentless Hunter. Two to four players divide a deck by suit, answer role-specific questions, and build conflicting histories until an ace triggers an ending shaped by predation, desperation, violence, and uncertain power.

title: Breathless SRD
synopsis: An open-licensed system reference document for tense stories of survival under relentless pressure. Characters roll step dice tied to broad skills, but every risky action degrades the die used until they can catch their breath; stress, limited supplies, stunts, and escalating danger support games where competence is temporary and survival never feels secure.

title: BUTT&HEAD
synopsis: A three-role fantasy adventure RPG in which two players control different halves of the same centaur while a Maestro presents the world and its challenges. A card system inspired by Go Fish and Blackjack powers checks and bargains, making communication, compromise, and the centaur's frequently conflicting impulses central to the journey.

title: By Moth or Moonlight
synopsis: A compact Wanderhome-inspired game for three to six players about animal-folk travelling through a gentle, changing world of nature, friendly insects, and forgotten spirits. Characters are built around heartfelt identities, small habits, relationships, and a single magical act, supporting GMless stories about friendship, healing, love, and change.

title: Cairn
synopsis: A rules-light fantasy adventure game built for dangerous exploration, meaningful choices, and fast rulings. Characters are defined by equipment and experience rather than classes, combat is direct and potentially deadly, and the Warden is encouraged to present clear information, visible danger, strange treasures, and problems that reward careful, creative play.

title: Cairn 2e Player’s Guide
synopsis: The player-facing core rules for Cairn's second edition, an adventure game about exploring a dark, mysterious Wood filled with strange people, hidden treasure, and dangerous creatures. It combines quick random character creation with inventory-driven play, tense expeditions, wilderness and dungeon procedures, advancement through experience, and fast, lethal combat.

title: Cairn 2e Warden’s Guide
synopsis: A companion toolkit for running Cairn second edition, focused on turning a few evocative ideas into a living adventure setting. It provides procedures and tables for factions, topography, settlements, forests, and dungeons, plus a bestiary, monster creation guidance, adventure design tools, and examples for preparing flexible situations rather than fixed plots.

title: Cairn Trouble in Twin Lakes
synopsis: A standalone Cairn second-edition adventure built around two connected mysteries in the low-fantasy region of Twin Lakes. The party explores several locations, meets competing NPCs and antagonists, and follows rumours and encounters surrounding a beloved butcher's disappearance, with material suitable for new characters and easy adaptation to another setting.

title: Call of Cthulhu A Cold Fire Within
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu A Cold Fire Within.jpg
synopsis: A Pulp Cthulhu campaign set in 1935, beginning with a missing-person investigation and escalating into a plot by time travellers to restore their lost empire. The heroes follow a trail from New York and the Catskills into K'n-yan, Yian-Ho, and the ancient past while trying to prevent an early awakening of the Great Old Ones.

title: Call of Cthulhu Alone Against the Dark
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Alone Against the Dark.jpg
synopsis: A globe-spanning solo Call of Cthulhu adventure set in 1931. The player investigates strange disappearances across New York, Greece, Egypt, Germany, and Antarctica, successively taking control of up to four prepared investigators as needed while racing to stop a calamity that could release an ancient city from the ice.

title: Call of Cthulhu Alone Against the Frost
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Alone Against the Frost.jpg
synopsis: A solo Call of Cthulhu adventure in which anthropologist L. C. Nadelmann leads a 1920s expedition into the uncharted North Hanninah region of Canada's Northwest Territories. Branching choices, investigation, survival, and Mythos danger determine whether the expedition achieves academic glory or vanishes into the frozen wilderness.

title: Call of Cthulhu Alone Against the Tide
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Alone Against the Tide.jpg
synopsis: A branching solo Call of Cthulhu mystery set in the remote lakeside town of Esbury, Massachusetts. Playing an original investigator or archaeologist Dr E. Woods, the reader follows leads connected to Professor William Harris, choosing paths through mist-shrouded streets whose consequences can alter both individual lives and the town's fate.

title: Call of Cthulhu Berlin the Wicked City
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Berlin the Wicked City.jpg
synopsis: A Call of Cthulhu setting book for Berlin during the turbulent years between the Great War and the Nazi rise to power. It supplies historical context, investigator and organisation guidance, notable people, locations, urban-generation tools, and three scenarios that can stand alone or form a campaign tracing the city's growing instability and horror.

title: Call of Cthulhu Dark Ages
synopsis: A historical horror setting that moves Call of Cthulhu to Anglo-Saxon England after the fall of Rome. It equips players and Keepers to create ordinary medieval investigators and confront witches, raiders, cults, restless dead, and Mythos terrors, with period professions, beliefs, equipment, setting material, rules adaptations, and scenarios for candlelit investigation.

title: Call of Cthulhu Dead Light and Other Dark Turns
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Dead Light and Other Dark Turns.jpg
synopsis: A collection of two roadside Call of Cthulhu scenarios and six shorter story seeds. Dead Light turns a chance meeting with a distressed woman into the aftermath of a terrible crime, while Saturnine Chalice traps stranded investigators in a deceptive house; both are designed for one or two sessions or insertion into a campaign.

title: Call of Cthulhu Does Love Forgive
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Does Love Forgive.jpg
synopsis: Two one-to-one Call of Cthulhu scenarios written for a single Keeper and player. Love You to Death begins with a missing dog in 1929 Chicago, while Mask of Desire unfolds amid a celebratory evening in 1930s Prague; each offers an intimate mystery designed to play over one or two sessions.

title: Call of Cthulhu Doors to Darkness
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Doors to Darkness.jpg
synopsis: A beginner-friendly anthology of five Call of Cthulhu investigations, supported by advice for new Keepers, pre-generated characters, handouts, and guidance on building mystery and horror. The scenarios range across buried secrets, sinister institutions, isolated lakes, unnatural family troubles, and a deadly substance spreading through a university town.

title: Call of Cthulhu Down Darker Trails
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Down Darker Trails.jpg
synopsis: A Call of Cthulhu sourcebook for mystery and Mythos horror in the American Old West. It provides period occupations, equipment, history, campaign guidance, locations ranging from frontier towns to the strange Shadow Desert, and two introductory adventures involving missing miners and a murder between feuding Texas ranches.

title: Call of Cthulhu Gateways to Terror
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Gateways to Terror.jpg
synopsis: An anthology of three short Call of Cthulhu scenarios designed to introduce mystery, investigation, and horror in sessions of around one to two hours. The Necropolis, What's in the Cellar?, and The Dead Boarder each include ready-made investigators, Keeper guidance, pacing advice, and a summary of the rules needed to play.

title: Call of Cthulhu Investigator Handbook
synopsis: A player-focused companion for Call of Cthulhu, expanding the tools for creating and portraying investigators. It offers extensive occupations and skills, optional creation rules, investigator organisations, historical context for the 1920s, equipment, advice on investigation and roleplaying, and a complete treatment of Lovecraft's The Dunwich Horror as inspiration.

title: Call of Cthulhu Keeper Rulebook
synopsis: The complete seventh-edition core rules for Call of Cthulhu, a game of ordinary investigators confronting cults, forbidden knowledge, and cosmic horrors that threaten sanity as readily as life. It covers character creation, skills, investigation, combat, chases, magic, the Mythos, Keeper guidance, creatures, spells, artefacts, and scenarios for beginning play.

title: Call of Cthulhu Keeper Tips
synopsis: A practical collection of advice for Call of Cthulhu Keepers, addressing the social and creative work of running horror games. Its short chapters cover establishing ground rules, inclusivity, preparation, pacing, clues, portraying non-player characters and monsters, using history, building atmosphere, managing campaigns, and adapting play when events move beyond the expected.

title: Call of Cthulhu Malleus Monstrorum Vol i - Monsters of the Mythos
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Malleus Monstrorum Vol i - Monsters of the Mythos.jpg
synopsis: The first volume of Call of Cthulhu's extensive Mythos bestiary, devoted to alien species, unnatural creatures, beasts, and horrors that investigators might encounter. Each entry supplies lore, variations, scenario inspiration, and seventh-edition game statistics, giving Keepers tools to present familiar entities in unexpected forms or introduce entirely new threats.

title: Call of Cthulhu Malleus Monstrorum Vol ii - Deities of the Mythos
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Malleus Monstrorum Vol ii - Deities of the Mythos.jpg
synopsis: The second Malleus Monstrorum volume, focused on Great Old Ones, Outer Gods, avatars, and other immense powers of the Cthulhu Mythos. It presents histories, cults, manifestations, powers, scenario ideas, and seventh-edition statistics, helping Keepers use cosmic entities as distant influences, active antagonists, or reality-altering forces within a campaign.

title: Call of Cthulhu Mansions of Madness
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Mansions of Madness.jpg
synopsis: A seventh-edition anthology of five Call of Cthulhu scenarios centred on houses, estates, and other places where private spaces conceal Mythos horror. Updated and newly written investigations take characters behind closed doors in the 1920s, supported by Keeper guidance, maps, handouts, and options for incorporating the stories into ongoing campaigns.

title: Call of Cthulhu Petersens Abominations
synopsis: Five modern-day Call of Cthulhu scenarios by Sandy Petersen, ranging from medical conspiracies and isolated hotels to deep drilling projects, strange communications, and a derelict ship. Designed for flexible use as convention games, standalone investigations, or campaign episodes, the collection includes pre-generated investigators, handouts, and guidance for adjusting each premise.

title: Call of Cthulhu Petersens Guide to Lovecraftian Horrors
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Petersens Guide to Lovecraftian Horrors.jpg
synopsis: An illustrated, system-neutral field guide to creatures from H. P. Lovecraft's fiction, written from the perspective of game designer Sandy Petersen. Detailed visual studies and commentary examine the anatomy, behaviour, scale, and unsettling qualities of numerous Mythos beings, offering inspiration for readers, artists, and horror roleplaying games without relying on statistics.

title: Call of Cthulhu Pulp Cthulhu
synopsis: A Call of Cthulhu supplement that reshapes cosmic horror into two-fisted 1930s pulp adventure. Tougher heroes, expanded talents, psychic abilities, weird science, altered luck and sanity rules, villain design, and campaign advice let investigators confront the Mythos more directly, while an included campaign demonstrates the heightened action and melodrama of the style.

title: Call of Cthulhu Quickstart Anniversary Edition
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Quickstart Anniversary Edition.jpg
synopsis: An anniversary edition of the Call of Cthulhu quick-start, providing streamlined seventh-edition rules, ready-made investigators, and The Haunting, the classic introductory scenario about a supposedly abandoned house. Additional historical and reflective material celebrates the game's development while giving a new group everything needed for an initial investigation.

title: Call of Cthulhu Reign of Terror
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Reign of Terror.jpg
synopsis: A Call of Cthulhu setting and scenario collection amid the violence and upheaval of the French Revolution. Historical guidance, occupations, timelines, maps, prepared investigators, and scenario seeds support independent play, while the linked adventures can also serve as a playable historical revelation connected to Horror on the Orient Express.

title: Call of Cthulhu Starter Set 1 Alone Against the Flames
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Starter Set 1 Alone Against the Flames.jpg
synopsis: A solo introductory Call of Cthulhu adventure that teaches the rules through play. Travelling to the isolated town of Emberhead in the 1920s, the reader creates an investigator, makes branching choices, and learns skills, characteristics, sanity, and combat while uncovering why the welcoming community is determined that its visitor should stay.

title: Call of Cthulhu Starter Set 2 Introductory Rules
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Starter Set 2 Introductory Rules.jpg
synopsis: The concise rules booklet from the Call of Cthulhu Starter Set, explaining how to create and play investigators in seventh edition. It introduces characteristics, skills, difficulty levels, bonus and penalty dice, sanity, combat, chases, improvement, and the Keeper's role, providing the mechanical foundation needed for the set's included scenarios.

title: Call of Cthulhu Starter Set 3 Scenarios
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu Starter Set 3 Scenarios.jpg
synopsis: Three progressively more involved Call of Cthulhu scenarios for new Keepers and players. Paper Chase offers an intimate one-on-one mystery, Edge of Darkness sends a group to confront a dead man's unfinished ritual, and Dead Man Stomp brings jazz-age investigation and supernatural violence, with guidance and handouts supporting each step.

title: Call of Cthulhu The Coloring Book
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu The Coloring Book.jpg
synopsis: A collection of 28 detailed illustrations by Andrey Fetisov for colouring, drawing on both Lovecraft’s fiction and classic Call of Cthulhu campaigns. Its scenes range from dreamlands and isolated New England communities to encounters inspired by The Dunwich Horror, Innsmouth, Masks of Nyarlathotep, and Horror on the Orient Express.

title: Call of Cthulhu The Grand Grimoire of Cthulhu Mythos Magic
cover: covers/ttrpg/Call of Cthulhu The Grand Grimoire of Cthulhu Mythos Magic.jpg
synopsis: An extensive seventh-edition compendium of Mythos magic for Call of Cthulhu and Pulp Cthulhu. It gathers hundreds of spells, variants, and magical traditions into one reference, while adding guidance on deeper magic, folk practices, spell learning, and the unsettling consequences of investigators or cultists tampering with forces beyond human understanding.

title: Campfire Scouts
synopsis: A game about children spending a week at summer camp, balancing ordinary daytime activities with supernatural threats that emerge after dark. Scouts build friendships, earn badges, and confront dangers from the Otherworld while managing mounting heat. The game deliberately leaves room to decide whether those horrors are real or products of imagination.

title: Candleberry Jam
synopsis: A system-neutral mystery set on Huzal, a remote island village sustained by its wondrous candlewood grove. When an outside speculator is found dead, visitors must navigate local relationships, competing plotlines, and the island’s past to uncover its secrets before old wrongdoing and new commercial pressure bring disaster to the community.

title: CBR+PNK
synopsis: A minimalist cyberpunk one-shot RPG about veteran runners undertaking one final high-stakes job in an oppressive, high-tech megacity. Its Forged in the Dark-inspired pamphlet rules focus on decisive engagement plans, mounting consequences, and improvisational play, supported by separate GM, character, and scenario framework sheets.

title: Christmas Cocaine Owlbear
synopsis: A chaotic one-shot inspired by Honey Heist in which woodland animals accidentally consume enchanted cocaine from a mauled courier and gain humanlike awareness. Their new intelligence reveals a much larger stash at the fallen North Pole, prompting an improvised Christmas heist full of unstable magic, criminal schemes, and dangerously overconfident animals.

title: Chronicle Connection Plus
synopsis: A solo journaling roleplaying game about love, friendship, and heartbreak, inspired by dating simulations and relationship-focused anime. Players create a protagonist and possible connections, then use a six-sided die, journal prompts, and changing relationship meters to discover special events, emotional turning points, and the uncertain course of each bond.

title: Cities Without Number Free Edition
synopsis: A complete cyberpunk sandbox roleplaying game about criminals, mercenaries, and outcasts surviving a corporate near-future. It combines lightweight old-school rules with extensive tools for creating cities, factions, missions, schemes, and technological threats. The system is broadly compatible with Stars Without Number and Worlds Without Number for cross-genre campaigns.

title: Citizen Sleeper Spindlejack
synopsis: A solo delivery game set in the world of Citizen Sleeper. As a spindlejack, you navigate Erlin’s Star’s cargo tunnels, choosing routes across a grid while balancing limited time, rising heat, and the danger of enormous haulers. Successful deliveries build reputation and open further work in the station’s hidden logistical underworld.

title: Cobwebs
synopsis: A GMless mystery game about grief, loss, and the cost of pursuing an uncomfortable truth. Three to five players take the roles of the Darling, the Shadow, and the Machine, following leads with light and dark dice. Their theories gradually shape the mystery until danger, sacrifice, and revelation bring the investigation to its end.

title: Creation Myths
synopsis: A solo character-creation and journaling tool that turns a new adventurer’s backstory into a sequence of reflective prompts. Following a familiar mythic narrative pattern, it explores the character’s origins, formative events, reactions, relationships, and eventual reason for joining a campaign, producing history that can be carried into another roleplaying game.

title: Cure Wounds Inc.
synopsis: A compact fantasy industrial dungeon set inside the Life Machine, the vast apparatus used by Cure Wounds Incorporated to mass-produce healing potions. Adventurers encounter exhausted workers, mutants, repair automata, and alchemical slimes while exploring the strange corporation that grew from a fish-and-chip shop into an indispensable part of its city.

title: CY_BORG
synopsis: A rules-light cyberpunk roleplaying game about desperate punks in the doomed city of Cy. Corporations, cults, ecological collapse, addictive technology, and casual violence define its hostile future. Built from the MÖRK BORG rules, it provides fast character creation, brutal d20 play, equipment, enemies, missions, and tools for improvising a collapsing urban nightmare.

title: CY_BORG Factions of Cy
synopsis: A third-party CY_BORG supplement introducing five thematic factions to the streets of Cy. Each organisation provides a distinct source of allies, enemies, jobs, and urban conflict, helping referees make the city’s competing interests more visible and giving punk crews new powers to bargain with, oppose, exploit, or become entangled in.

title: CY_BORG Forty Foes Bestiary
synopsis: An independent CY_BORG-compatible bestiary containing forty game-ready adversaries drawn from Cy’s slums, gang wars, quarantined districts, and consumer wastelands. Each foe offers a compact threat for immediate play, giving game masters a varied supply of violent residents, altered creatures, corporate hazards, and other problems to drop into missions.

title: CY_BORG Kill ENGN
synopsis: A mech-focused supplement for CY_BORG that adds pilots, modular machines, and rules for assembling and fighting with mechanized systems. It expands street-level cyberpunk play into heavier tactical confrontations while retaining the parent game’s speed and brutality, with corporate hardware, interchangeable parts, hazardous weather, and tools for creating customised combat platforms.

title: CY_BORG Kill ENGN - Cast Oubliette
synopsis: A mechanized sludge-crawl adventure for CY_BORG and the Kill ENGN mech rules. It sends crews through the polluted districts and ruins of Mosscroft and Little Hell, where hackerspaces, fighting venues, hostile machines, and local factions turn an urban operation into a grimy exploration of industrial decay and improvised mechanized violence.

title: CY_BORG The 55
synopsis: A CY_BORG location sourcebook detailing Stack 95563, known as the 55: a 365-floor arcology designed to function as a city unto itself. Its sharply divided districts, corporate services, residents, and concealed infrastructure provide a dense vertical setting, accompanied by situations and mission hooks that can pull crews throughout the Stack.

title: cyan starlight
synopsis: A solo science-fiction game about the last human awakening a hundred thousand years late to a galaxy washed in blue-green light. Using Breathless-style degrading dice, the traveller keeps a failing ship moving between systems, explores worlds, gathers clues to humanity’s disappearance, resists despair, and works toward one of hundreds of possible endings.

title: Cybermetal 2012
synopsis: A cyberpunk roleplaying game set in Pentagram City, where citizens survive under a single law amid gangs, invasive technology, violent media, and demonic influence. Players create hardware-enhanced humans, demons, vermin, or husks, using a charged dice system for conflicts, surgery, crafting, reputation, raids, and other dangers of its feverish retro-future.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Blackhand’s Street Weapons
synopsis: A consolidated Cyberpunk 2020 armoury containing more than 250 weapons collected from across the game line. Entries are organised by type, from melee weapons and handguns to heavy weapons, explosives, ammunition, and full-conversion cyborg armaments. The compilation incorporates accumulated corrections and also gathers recoil and specialised ammunition rules for easy reference.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Brainware Blowout
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 equipment and rules supplement devoted to Netrunners and their trade. It expands the tools available for working the global Net with cyberdecks, programs, hardware, upgrades, and related technology, gathering material from earlier sourcebooks alongside new options for characters whose information warfare and virtual infiltration matter as much as street combat.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Chrome 1-2
synopsis: A combined collection of the first two Chromebook equipment supplements for Cyberpunk 2020. It catalogues the consumer technology and status symbols of 2020, including electronics, vehicles, cyberware, weapons, fashion, chipware, housing, software, and specialist services. The entries provide both character options and ready-made details for building Night City scenes and adventure hooks.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Chrome 3-4
synopsis: A combined collection of the third and fourth Chromebook equipment supplements for Cyberpunk 2020. It expands the setting’s catalogue with clothing, pharmaceuticals, cyberware, vehicles, computers, software, cyberpets, robots, full-body conversions, powered armour, and maintenance rules, offering a broad selection of upgrades and complications for characters, corporations, and campaigns.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Core Rulebook
synopsis: The second-edition core game of corporate power, street survival, and cybernetic ambition in the dark future of Night City. It provides character roles ranging from Solos and Netrunners to Medias, Nomads, and Fixers, together with rules for combat, cyberware, hacking, equipment, advancement, and running intense urban stories at the edge of collapse.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Corporation Report
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook examining the setting’s powerful multinational corporations from the perspective of the people who serve, oppose, and profit from them. It details corporate structures, resources, personnel, rivalries, and covert operations, giving referees organisations that can act as employers, enemies, patrons, or the hidden machinery behind a campaign’s conflicts.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Deep Space
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 supplement extending the dark future beyond Earth into orbit and the wider solar system. It covers space habitats, factions, environmental hazards, zero-gravity combat, spacecraft, travel, communications, equipment, and weapons, providing the technical and setting material needed for campaigns among lunar settlements, orbital installations, and remote deep-space operations.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Edgerunners Inc
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook about professional mercenaries who take dangerous jobs on the edge of legality. It presents an organisation that connects clients with capable teams, along with campaign structures, contracts, contacts, equipment, and complications for running mission-driven games in which reputation and survival depend on delivering results.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Eurosource Plus
synopsis: A regional sourcebook for Cyberpunk 2020 describing Europe in the dark future. It surveys the continent’s nations, political blocs, corporations, cultures, conflicts, and technology, highlighting how European life differs from Night City. The material supports travel, espionage, corporate intrigue, and campaigns rooted in a wealthy but sharply divided international power centre.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Eurotour
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 campaign following a major rock tour across Europe. Performers, security personnel, and other edgerunners face the pressures of celebrity, politics, media manipulation, and organised violence as the tour moves between cities. The linked scenarios combine concert logistics and cultural detail with threats capable of turning public spectacle into disaster.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Firestorm Shockwave
synopsis: The concluding volume of the Firestorm campaign for Cyberpunk 2020, depicting the escalating Fourth Corporate War and its devastating effect on Night City. It provides major events, military operations, factions, equipment, and scenarios for characters caught between corporate armies as covert conflict becomes open warfare and the setting approaches a historic breaking point.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Firestorm Stormfront
synopsis: The opening volume of the Firestorm campaign for Cyberpunk 2020, chronicling the beginning of the Fourth Corporate War. It details the rival corporations, international battlefields, military hardware, and covert operations that draw edgerunners into an expanding conflict, providing both campaign background and missions tied to the war’s dangerous early stages.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Guide to the NET
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook presenting the global Net as a place to explore rather than a purely abstract computer system. Written in the voice of legendary Netrunner Rache Bartmoss, it maps regions, systems, organisations, personalities, programs, and dangers, expanding virtual adventures and the wider culture surrounding hacking in the dark future.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Home of the Brave
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook surveying the fractured United States after economic collapse, political upheaval, and environmental disaster. It details regions, cities, institutions, travel, everyday life, and national power structures beyond Night City, giving referees a broader setting for road campaigns, political stories, and adventures across the recovering country.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Land of the Free
synopsis: A cross-country Cyberpunk 2020 campaign that takes an edgerunner team across the divided United States while protecting a valuable young passenger. The journey links varied locations, factions, and dangers from coast to coast, using the wider American setting for a sustained pursuit filled with corporate interests, hostile forces, and difficult alliances.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Listen Up You Primitive Screwheads
cover: covers/ttrpg/Cyberpunk 2020 Listen Up You Primitive Screwheads.jpg
synopsis: A referee’s advice book for Cyberpunk 2020 focused on running sharper, more convincing dark-future campaigns. It discusses atmosphere, rules judgement, character roles, group management, adventure design, opposition, and the consequences of violence, offering practical techniques for challenging capable players while preserving the setting’s speed, danger, and attitude.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Live and Direct
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook devoted to Medias, Rockerboys, celebrity, and mass communication. It expands broadcasting, journalism, entertainment, propaganda, and public influence, with character options, equipment, organisations, and campaign ideas for stories where controlling the message can matter as much as winning a firefight.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Maximum Metal
synopsis: A heavy-combat supplement for Cyberpunk 2020 covering tanks, armoured vehicles, aircraft, powered armour, and other military hardware. It adds rules for operating and fighting with large machines, along with weapons and equipment suited to battlefield-scale action, allowing campaigns to move beyond street skirmishes into corporate and military warfare.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Neo Tribes
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook about Nomads and the mobile nations that cross a damaged America. It describes their families, cultures, occupations, vehicles, routes, and rivalries, expanding the Nomad role and presenting communities whose transport networks and practical skills make them vital players beyond the security of established cities.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Night City
synopsis: A detailed city sourcebook for Cyberpunk 2020, mapping the neighbourhoods, businesses, gangs, corporations, landmarks, and dangers of Night City. It provides locations and local personalities for street-level play, enabling referees to build missions around the social geography of the game’s central metropolis rather than treating it as a generic urban backdrop.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Pacific Rim
synopsis: A regional Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook covering the nations and economies around the Pacific. It surveys cultures, corporations, politics, technology, and conflicts across a rapidly changing region, providing setting detail and campaign material for edgerunners working amid powerful states, dense cities, organised crime, and intense corporate competition.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Protect and Serve
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook focused on police officers, law enforcement agencies, and the compromises of maintaining order in the dark future. It expands the Cop role with procedures, organisations, equipment, investigations, and campaign advice for stories about corruption, public pressure, violent crime, and policing communities dominated by corporate power.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Rockerboy
synopsis: A Cyberpunk sourcebook centred on musicians, performers, rebels, and the power of culture as political action. It explores the Rockerboy role, the music industry, bands, venues, media, equipment, and campaigns built around fame and resistance, showing how a compelling voice can mobilise crowds and threaten entrenched authority.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Rough Guide to the UK
cover: covers/ttrpg/Cyberpunk 2020 Rough Guide to the UK.jpg
synopsis: A regional Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook presenting the United Kingdom in the dark future. It outlines government, corporations, cities, subcultures, security, technology, and everyday conditions across the country, supplying locations, factions, and campaign ideas for British stories shaped by surveillance, inequality, tradition, and rapid social change.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Solo of Fortune
synopsis: A Cyberpunk sourcebook for Solos and other professional combatants, written in the style of a mercenary magazine. It provides weapons, equipment, tactics, personalities, organisations, and reports from global conflicts, combining practical character options with setting material for campaigns involving security work, military operations, and hired violence.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Tales from the Forlorn Hope
cover: covers/ttrpg/Cyberpunk 2020 Tales from the Forlorn Hope.jpg
synopsis: A collection of linked Cyberpunk 2020 scenarios centred on the Forlorn Hope, a Night City bar frequented by veterans and mercenaries. Its missions draw characters into the personal troubles and unfinished business of the regulars, creating a campaign where relationships, loyalty, and past wars matter alongside dangerous professional work.

title: Cyberpunk 2020 Wildside
synopsis: A Cyberpunk 2020 sourcebook devoted to Fixers, the brokers and dealmakers who connect Night City’s people, goods, and opportunities. It expands contacts, reputation, markets, criminal networks, and negotiation, giving players and referees tools for campaigns driven by favours, information, scarce resources, and the social machinery behind every successful job.

title: Cyberpunk RED
synopsis: The core roleplaying game of the Time of the Red, set after a corporate war has shattered global systems and left Night City rebuilding amid scarcity. Players become skilled edgerunners taking dangerous work, with rules for roles, combat, Netrunning, cyberware, equipment, downtime, reputation, and running campaigns in a volatile urban recovery.

title: Cyberpunk RED Black Chrome
synopsis: An equipment sourcebook for Cyberpunk RED presenting the vehicles, weapons, cyberware, electronics, clothing, and services available to discerning edgerunners. Framed through the city’s night markets and vendors, it expands character options while showing how commerce, scarcity, branding, and street reputation shape everyday life in the Time of the Red.

title: Cyberpunk RED Black Chrome+
synopsis: A free digital companion to Black Chrome containing additional Cyberpunk RED equipment and supporting material. It extends the main book’s catalogue with more products, options, and context for Night City’s markets, giving players new purchases to pursue and referees further technology to place in shops, rewards, and jobs.

title: Cyberpunk RED Danger Gal Dossier
synopsis: A Cyberpunk RED collection of ready-to-use non-player characters and factions assembled as an in-world intelligence dossier. It provides backgrounds, relationships, motivations, equipment, and game statistics for people across Night City, helping referees populate campaigns with allies, rivals, crews, and recurring threats tied to the setting’s organisations.

title: Cyberpunk RED Hot Pursuit
synopsis: A Cyberpunk RED rules supplement for high-speed chases and vehicle encounters. It expands driving beyond a single check with procedures for pursuit, manoeuvres, hazards, crashes, and combat on the move, giving Nomads and other edgerunners a structured way to stage escapes, interceptions, and dangerous races through Night City.

title: Cyberpunk RED Interface RED Vol 1
synopsis: A Cyberpunk RED compilation collecting articles and game material originally released digitally. It gathers character options, equipment, encounters, creatures, and rules expansions into a single reference, including material that broadens both street-level adventures and the stranger technological possibilities of the Time of the Red.

title: Cyberpunk RED Interface RED Vol 2
synopsis: The second Cyberpunk RED compilation of digital articles, optional systems, equipment, and setting material. It consolidates varied additions for players and referees into one volume, providing new tools, threats, character choices, and pieces of Night City life that can be introduced individually or woven into an ongoing campaign.

title: Cyberpunk RED Interface RED Vol 3
synopsis: The third Cyberpunk RED compilation of digital supplements, collecting further rules, equipment, characters, and setting material. Designed as a practical expansion library, it gives groups additional options and ready-to-use content for jobs in Night City while preserving the core game’s focus on scarcity, style, and dangerous professional work.

title: Cyberpunk RED Jumpstart Kit Worldbook
synopsis: The setting half of the Cyberpunk RED Jumpstart Kit, introducing Night City and the Time of the Red to new groups. It explains the aftermath of the Fourth Corporate War, everyday street life, major forces, technology, and locations, while supplying introductory material and scenario support for beginning a campaign.

title: Cyberpunk RED Night City Tarot
synopsis: A Cyberpunk RED accessory built around a tarot deck illustrated through the people, symbols, and dangers of Night City. The cards function as a thematic artefact and a source of inspiration at the table, helping generate characters, situations, imagery, fortunes, and interpretations suited to stories in the Time of the Red.

title: Cyberpunk RED Tales of the Red
cover: covers/ttrpg/Cyberpunk RED Tales of the Red.jpg
synopsis: A collection of full-length missions for Cyberpunk RED set across Night City during the Time of the Red. The scenarios present varied clients, locations, adversaries, and complications, and can be played separately or linked through an edgerunner crew’s developing reputation, relationships, and involvement in the city’s recovery.

title: Cyberpunk RED Tales of the Red+
cover: covers/ttrpg/Cyberpunk RED Tales of the Red+.jpg
synopsis: A companion volume expanding Tales of the Red with extra Cyberpunk RED material connected to its missions. It supplies additional characters, locations, equipment, and play aids that deepen the anthology’s jobs and aftermath, helping referees revisit its people and consequences or develop them into a broader campaign.

title: Cycles and Loops - The Midrange
synopsis: A design reference collecting flowcharted tabletop roleplaying procedures that operate at the middle scale of play, such as combat turns and other repeatable subsystems. Each procedure adapts ideas from one or more games into a broadly reusable form, encouraging designers to study, combine, mechanise, and connect them within larger structures of play.

title: Cycles of the Eye
synopsis: A tarot-driven solo game set on Erlin’s Eye in the Citizen Sleeper universe. As an artificial Sleeper escaping corporate ownership, the player assigns daily energy dice to jobs and challenges while a decaying body reduces their options. Cards reveal locations, residents, adversaries, and a final story of escape or belonging.

title: D&D Bonfire - A Long Rest Supplement
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Bonfire - A Long Rest Supplement.jpg
synopsis: A Dungeons & Dragons supplement that makes long rests into scenes rather than simple bookkeeping. It offers prompts and procedures for characters gathering around a fire, reflecting on recent events, sharing stories, and strengthening relationships, giving quieter moments of travel and recovery a clearer role in the rhythm of an adventure.

title: D&D Codex of the Infinite Planes - Plane of Water
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Codex of the Infinite Planes - Plane of Water.jpg
synopsis: A planar supplement for Dungeons & Dragons focused on the Elemental Plane of Water. It provides setting material, locations, inhabitants, hazards, encounters, and adventure ideas for an oceanic realm without a conventional surface, supporting expeditions through strange seas and campaigns involving elemental powers and planar travel.

title: D&D Curse of Strahd
synopsis: A gothic horror campaign for Dungeons & Dragons in which adventurers become trapped in Barovia, a mist-bound realm ruled by the vampire Count Strahd von Zarovich. Players explore haunted communities and ruined places, gather allies and relics, and confront Strahd’s influence in a flexible campaign shaped by tragedy, temptation, and an unpredictable reading of fortunes.

title: D&D Dungeon Master’s Guide
synopsis: The core Dungeons & Dragons guide for preparing and running games. It explains campaign and adventure creation, adjudicating rules, building encounters, designing worlds, handling treasure and magic items, and adapting the system with optional rules, giving Dungeon Masters both practical procedures and a broad toolkit for shaping play.

title: D&D Journeys Through the Radiant Citadel
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Journeys Through the Radiant Citadel.jpg
synopsis: An anthology of Dungeons & Dragons adventures connected by the Radiant Citadel, a refuge in the Ethereal Plane linked to diverse civilisations. Each scenario presents a distinct setting inspired by real-world cultures and their creators’ experiences, while the Citadel supplies a recurring home base for travel, community, and continuing campaigns.

title: D&D One Night Strahd
synopsis: A condensed, remixable reimagining of Curse of Strahd designed to deliver its gothic conflict in a single extended session or short campaign. It restructures Castle Ravenloft and the surrounding story into a focused sequence of encounters, mysteries, and confrontations, with modular paths that let groups tailor the night’s intensity and complexity.

title: D&D Player’s Handbook
synopsis: The primary player reference for Dungeons & Dragons, containing the rules needed to create characters and take part in fantasy adventures. It presents ancestries, classes, backgrounds, equipment, spells, exploration, social interaction, and combat, alongside guidance for developing a character whose abilities and personality grow throughout a campaign.

title: D&D Radiant Citadel - 01 Salted Legacy DM Pack
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Radiant Citadel - 01 Salted Legacy DM Pack.jpg
synopsis: A Dungeon Master support pack for Salted Legacy, the opening adventure in Journeys Through the Radiant Citadel. It organises scenario information and provides practical play aids for running the bustling night market, its rival families, competitions, investigation, and social encounters with less preparation at the table.

title: D&D Radiant Citadel - 02 Written in Blood DM Pack
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Radiant Citadel - 02 Written in Blood DM Pack.jpg
synopsis: A Dungeon Master support pack for Written in Blood from Journeys Through the Radiant Citadel. It prepares the adventure’s locations, characters, clues, encounters, and horror elements for ready reference, helping the table follow a rural community’s celebration into an investigation of violence, memory, and buried history.

title: D&D Radiant Citadel - 03 Fiend of Hollow Mine DM Pack
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Radiant Citadel - 03 Fiend of Hollow Mine DM Pack.jpg
synopsis: A Dungeon Master support pack for Fiend of Hollow Mine from Journeys Through the Radiant Citadel. It gathers the scenario’s locations, non-player characters, encounters, and investigative information into practical aids for running a pursuit through a festival city threatened by disappearances, corruption, and a supernatural foe.

title: D&D Radiant Citadel - 04 Wages of Vice DM Pack
cover: covers/ttrpg/D&D Radiant Citadel - 04 Wages of Vice DM Pack.jpg
synopsis: A Dungeon Master support pack for Wages of Vice from Journeys Through the Radiant Citadel. It presents the mystery’s people, places, clues, and encounters in a table-ready format, supporting a murder investigation amid celebration, political tension, personal grudges, and the dangerous consequences of an old injustice.

title: D&D Sword Coast Adventurer’s Guide
synopsis: A Dungeons & Dragons setting guide to the Sword Coast and surrounding regions of the Forgotten Realms. It surveys cities, nations, factions, history, religion, and everyday life, while adding character backgrounds and options rooted in the setting, giving players and Dungeon Masters context for adventures across Faerûn’s best-known western lands.

title: D&D Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything
synopsis: A Dungeons & Dragons expansion containing character options, spells, magic items, puzzles, and Dungeon Master tools presented with commentary from the archmage Tasha. It adds subclasses and flexible approaches to character creation while broadening rules for group patrons, environmental hazards, sidekicks, and other ways to shape campaigns.

title: D&D The Wolves of Langston
synopsis: A solo Dungeons & Dragons adventure built around an investigation in the town of Langston. Designed for a single player character, it uses guided choices, skill checks, combat, and clues to uncover the cause of a local threat, providing a structured roleplaying experience without requiring a Dungeon Master.

title: D&D Tomb of Annihilation
synopsis: A Dungeons & Dragons campaign of jungle exploration and deadly dungeon delving centred on the peninsula of Chult. Adventurers race to end a curse that prevents resurrection and drains the previously restored, navigating lost settlements, hostile wilderness, rival expeditions, and an infamous tomb engineered to test intruders with traps and monsters.

title: D&D Uncaged Volume 1
synopsis: An anthology of Dungeons & Dragons adventures that reinterprets mythological women and female monsters beyond their traditional roles. Its scenarios present figures such as hags, harpies, and medusas with varied motives and perspectives, offering encounters that emphasise agency, context, and choices more complicated than simply identifying and defeating a monster.

title: D&D Xanathar’s Guide to Everything
synopsis: A Dungeons & Dragons expansion framed by observations from the beholder crime lord Xanathar. It provides subclasses, spells, feats, encounter tools, downtime systems, traps, and Dungeon Master guidance, expanding both character development and campaign preparation with optional rules and reference material for many common situations at the table.

title: Dark Heresy Genesys
synopsis: A fan adaptation that brings Warhammer 40,000’s Dark Heresy setting to the Genesys roleplaying system. It supplies character creation, careers, skills, talents, equipment, psychic powers, adversaries, and setting rules for agents of the Inquisition investigating heresy, corruption, and alien threats across the oppressive Imperium of Man.

title: Deathmatch Island
synopsis: A cinematic roleplaying game about contestants trapped in a deadly reality-television competition on a mysterious island. Players survive escalating challenges, shifting alliances, production manipulation, and violent eliminations while uncovering what lies behind the show. Its campaign structure draws on conspiracy thrillers, battle royales, and the artificial drama of televised entertainment.

title: Delta Green A Night at the Opera
cover: covers/ttrpg/Delta Green A Night at the Opera.jpg
synopsis: A collection of Delta Green operations in which government agents confront unnatural threats hidden within modern life. The scenarios can stand alone or form a campaign, moving from disturbing investigations into increasingly dangerous encounters where secrecy, compromised institutions, and the psychological cost of the mission are as threatening as the entities involved.

title: Delta Green Agent’s Handbook
synopsis: The player-facing core rules for Delta Green, a modern conspiracy-horror game about agents secretly combating the unnatural. It covers character creation, professions, skills, bonds, combat, sanity, equipment, and investigative play, establishing how operatives balance dangerous assignments with the personal relationships and ordinary lives those assignments steadily erode.

title: Delta Green Archint
synopsis: A Delta Green sourcebook presenting archaeological intelligence files: sites, artefacts, and past discoveries connected to the unnatural. Its case material spans different places and periods, giving Handlers historical mysteries, operational seeds, and dangerous evidence that can be investigated directly or woven into campaigns about institutions repeatedly uncovering what should remain buried.

title: Delta Green Black Sites
synopsis: A collection of Delta Green scenarios and support material focused on hidden facilities, compromised operations, and unnatural incidents. The missions place agents in varied modern investigations where official authority offers limited protection, and where containing evidence, protecting secrecy, and surviving the consequences may be incompatible goals.

title: Delta Green Conspiracy
synopsis: A sourcebook for running Delta Green during the 1990s, when the organisation exists as an illegal conspiracy within the United States government. It details the era’s agencies, operations, tradecraft, technology, adversaries, and hidden history, recreating the original game’s atmosphere of paranoia while using the current rules and setting framework.

title: Delta Green Control Group
synopsis: A collection of introductory Delta Green scenarios that places ordinary government and military personnel in their first encounters with the unnatural. The operations demonstrate the game’s investigative structure, institutional pressures, violence, and sanity costs, and can culminate in surviving characters being drawn together for a continuing covert campaign.

title: Delta Green God’s Teeth
synopsis: A Delta Green campaign about agents assigned to a horrifying case whose consequences resurface years later. The investigation spans trauma, institutional failure, moral injury, and unnatural predation, forcing the team to confront what their earlier actions enabled and whether the programme they serve can distinguish containment from complicity.

title: Delta Green Handler’s Guide
synopsis: The Handler-facing core book for Delta Green, providing the secret history and unnatural cosmology behind the game. It includes guidance for creating and running investigations, adversaries, artefacts, rituals, organisations, and campaign structures, equipping the referee to portray both cosmic horror and the bureaucratic machinery that attempts to contain it.

title: Delta Green Iconoclasts
synopsis: A Delta Green campaign set amid the conflict in Iraq, where a disastrous encounter with the unnatural draws agents into a race against spreading catastrophe. It combines intelligence work, regional politics, military danger, and occult investigation, asking the team to identify and contain a threat while operating inside a complex contemporary war.

title: Delta Green Impossible Landscapes
synopsis: A surreal horror campaign for Delta Green centred on the King in Yellow and a reality-eroding mystery that unfolds across decades. Agents follow recurring people, places, documents, and impossible architecture as an old investigation contaminates the present, turning procedural certainty into obsession and making the boundaries of identity, time, and truth increasingly unreliable.

title: Delta Green Need to Know
synopsis: An introductory Delta Green package containing essential rules, pregenerated agents, and the operation Last Things Last. It teaches the game through a seemingly simple task involving a deceased operative’s affairs, allowing a new group to experience investigation, secrecy, difficult decisions, and the personal cost of encountering the unnatural.

title: Delta Green Static Protocol
synopsis: A Handler’s reference for Impossible Landscapes that organises its recurring clues, entities, locations, timelines, and interpretations. It is designed to help manage the campaign’s deliberately tangled structure, making connections easier to track while offering additional context and guidance for presenting its surreal mysteries coherently at the table.

title: Delta Green The Complex
synopsis: A sourcebook of organisations and professions for Delta Green characters drawn from the modern national-security state and related institutions. It details agencies, contractors, law enforcement bodies, and specialised careers, providing backgrounds, skills, authorities, and complications for agents whose official work gives them access to unnatural investigations.

title: Delta Green The Labyrinth
synopsis: A Delta Green campaign sourcebook presenting interlinked allies, antagonists, organisations, and ongoing threats. Rather than a linear adventure, it offers a network of people and conspiracies that react to agents over time, allowing Handlers to build a personalised campaign in which relationships deepen, collide, and produce lasting consequences.

title: Dice Hard
synopsis: A fast, zero-preparation roleplaying game where characters must solve each problem in a new way. Distinct actions earn dice for an expanding damage pool, building toward one spectacular confrontation with a wildly generated final monster. It is designed to teach itself during play and produce a complete, comic adventure in roughly an hour.

title: Die Grave Robber Die
synopsis: A Trophy Dark incursion set in a Victorian-flavoured community after respected townsfolk discover a newly occupied grave has been emptied by robbers. A professional mourner, groundskeeper, and other desperate pursuers follow the stolen corpse into escalating desecration, body horror, manipulation, and grim revelation, where the theft is only the day’s first atrocity.

title: DIE RPG
synopsis: A fantasy-horror roleplaying game based on the comic DIE. Players first create flawed people in the real world, then portray the powerful Paragons they become when dragged into a fantasy realm shaped by their hopes, fears, and gaming history. Returning home requires agreement, making desire and damaged relationships as important as adventure.

title: DMocracy
synopsis: A one-page murder-mystery game about bad workers and worse management. Its compact rules turn workplace hierarchy, resentment, incompetence, and suspicion into a rapidly improvised investigation, giving a group just enough structure to establish the victim, expose the organisation’s dysfunction, and determine which employee or manager is responsible.

title: Do Not Adjust Your Set
synopsis: An anthology of six system-flexible horror scenarios inspired by urban legends, campus stories, historical panics, and creepypasta. Its investigations involve haunted media, dangerous desires, strange fraternities, phantom attackers, and other modern folklore, providing adaptable mysteries that can be placed into contemporary supernatural campaigns or run as unsettling standalone stories.

title: Dream Askew - Dream Apart
synopsis: Two GMless games of marginalised communities maintaining belonging in precarious worlds. Dream Askew follows a queer enclave amid societal collapse, while Dream Apart explores Jewish life in a fantastical shtetl. Both distribute setting authority among players through roles, moves, and tokens, and include guidance for facilitating and designing further Belonging Outside Belonging games.

title: Eat the Reich
synopsis: A fast, violent action-horror game in which a squad of vampire commandos is dropped into occupied Paris with a simple objective: drink Adolf Hitler’s blood. Players tear through Nazi forces, supernatural weapons, and escalating set pieces using a system built for cinematic destruction, teamwork, and missions that become bloodier and more spectacular as they advance.

title: Echo of Ghosts
synopsis: A roleplaying game about ghosts who break into the living world to reclaim objects stolen from their community. Crews pass through inconvenient doors between worlds, evade specialised looters and predatory wraiths, and use their ghostly natures to track each target, turning a supernatural retrieval job into a tense heist shaped by memory and loss.

title: Eldritch Automata Quicklaunch Guide
synopsis: An introductory guide to Eldritch Automata, a post-apocalyptic game in which pilots bond with powerful machines to defend surviving communities from eldritch threats. It presents a streamlined first experience of the setting and system, combining personal relationships, psychological strain, and dramatic mechanised combat in a world rebuilding after the arrival of the Architect.

title: Escape From Neo-Millenia
synopsis: A prototype GMless cyberpunk adventure playable solo or collaboratively in a choose-your-own-path format. Players select a compact stat block, manage limited electrical juice, and make branching decisions using two six-sided dice. Prompts build the city of Neo-Millennia during play, while recorded page choices allow later events to alter earlier decisions.

title: ExNovo
synopsis: A collaborative city-building game for one to four players that creates a usable settlement map and history in about two hours. Players act as guardian spirits, guiding a community from its founding through development and transformation while adding terrain, districts, landmarks, factions, resources, and events that make the finished city suitable for stories or other games.

title: Fabula Ultima Press Start
synopsis: A guided tutorial adventure for Fabula Ultima, designed to teach the game’s JRPG-inspired rules through play. Pregenerated heroes and a structured sequence of scenes introduce exploration, conflicts, bonds, character abilities, and collaborative storytelling step by step, allowing a new group to begin without first studying the full core rulebook.

title: Fallen From Grace
synopsis: A solo tarot-driven journaling game about morality, redemption, and failure. You play an angel cast from Heaven into a human body, given one chance to earn a return while earthly temptations pull toward Hell. Daily devotions, grace, and all 78 tarot cards prompt the character’s choices, reflections, setbacks, and possible fate.

title: Fight Card System
synopsis: A design guide and system reference for creating tabletop fighting games in the style of Transgender Deathmatch Legend. One player controls a protagonist moving across a map while a facilitator portrays the world and opponents. Combat uses a standard deck and trick-taking procedure, with commentary on adapting the structure for new games and supplements.

title: Fire & Stone
synopsis: A Stone Age player supplement designed for Knave and readily adaptable to other old-school games. Inspired by prehistory and animist belief, it offers character backgrounds, three cultures, equipment packages, weapons, survival gear, random tables, and a setting of stone, grit, caves, spirits, and strange creatures beyond the explored horizon.

title: FIST
synopsis: A paranormal mercenary roleplaying game set during an alternate late twentieth-century cold war. Players create exceptional soldiers of fortune sent on covert missions involving experimental weapons, cryptids, psychic phenomena, and impossible technology. Lightweight rules, modular traits, and mission-building tools support fast operations inspired by action teams, espionage fiction, and tactical videogames.

title: Fukuzatsu+
synopsis: An expanded edition of Fukuzatsu, a competitive card game whose title means “complicated.” Players navigate a deliberately cutthroat contest steeped in mystery, reading opponents and managing the changing possibilities of the shared cards. The additional material broadens the original design while preserving its focus on tense, deceptive play.

title: Gentleman Bandit
synopsis: A solo writing game about an eloquent highwayman who leaves a thirteen-line poem at the scene of every robbery. Using playing cards and optional dice, the player composes each increasingly revealing verse while discovering the bandit’s heart, crimes, reputation, and fate, blending procedural poetry with the romantic and violent mythology of the road.

title: Grail Trail
synopsis: A compact 24XX questing game about pilgrims pursuing a Grail through dangerous missions. Characters act through risk-based skill rolls, improve by demonstrating virtue, and share access to a developing Avatar. Its lightweight rules emphasise purposeful journeys, moral choices, collaborative interpretation, and the ways a sacred quest changes both travellers and the world around them.

title: GRID BEEF - A Racing RPG
synopsis: A roleplaying game about world-championship motor racing, where drivers compete on the track while players collaborate on the drama surrounding them. Races create strategic pressure and uncertain results; between events, friendships, rivalries, politics, and media narratives develop. The game embraces heightened technology and raw emotion, ensuring that losing can still produce compelling stories.

title: Habitation
synopsis: A science-fiction exploration game about crews crossing dangerous environments to make discoveries, complete missions, and escape corporate debt. Players and the game master build a shared map from tagged locations, then confront scarcity and disruption during expeditions. Its focus rests on the explorers’ collective journey and the story of survival rather than individual character optimisation.

title: Hapsy Kordo
synopsis: An adventure structured around four rival restaurants awaiting a visit from the formidable critic Hapsy Kordo. Players choose tasks for each establishment before his fourth-day tour, dealing with staff, guests, mishaps, and competing interests. Their successes and failures reshape the district and determine which culinary ambitions survive the critic’s appetite and judgement.

title: Heart - The City Beneath
synopsis: A fantasy-horror roleplaying game about doomed delvers descending into the Heart, a reality-warping undercity beneath Spire. Characters pursue impossible desires through unstable landmarks, strange communities, monsters, and transformative fallout. The resistance-based rules drive expeditions toward dramatic consequences, allowing each adventurer’s calling to grant fulfilment, ruin, or both.

title: Heart Burned and Broken
synopsis: A conversion guide for bringing characters and campaigns from Spire into Heart: The City Beneath. It explains how former Ministry agents fall into the undercity, translates Spire’s advances and identities into Heart origins and callings, and supplies material for continuing revolutionary stories among Derelictus, the Vermissian, and the Ministry’s operations below.

title: Heavy Weighs the Crown
synopsis: A solo journaling game played from the perspective of a magical crown guiding generations of monarchs. Structured prompts follow a realm from hopeful founding through its age of glory to inevitable ruin, recording how rulers, legacies, political choices, mundane subversion, and supernatural calamity reshape both the kingdom and the symbol of authority that outlives them.

title: Hello Stranger
synopsis: A live-action online game centred on an evolving connection between two people. Music and structured digital communication become prompts for creating their shared story, with guidance for setup, safety, synchronous scenes, and asynchronous play. Its flexible framework can support romance or other intimate relationships across genres, including stories of idols or spies.

title: Here, There, Be Monsters!
synopsis: A rules-light, queer, antifascist game that reverses monster-hunting fiction. Players create anomalous or monstrous people protecting one another from institutions and hunters who would exploit or destroy them. Tag-based characters, two-die resolution, collaborative worldbuilding, and extensive tables support supernatural communities that fight back rather than accept the role of targets.

title: Hive of the Crawling Creeps
synopsis: A system-light body-horror dungeon centred on a subterranean hive of flesh-eating insects. It maps organic tunnels and chambers, from spawning pools to the royal chamber, and supplies varied creep forms, prisoners, loot, and environmental details. The creatures’ pheromonal creepstink makes their behaviour and the hive’s escalating response part of the threat.

title: Hunter- The Reckoning
synopsis: A World of Darkness roleplaying game about ordinary people who recognise supernatural predators and choose to fight back. Hunters form a cell, investigate monsters hidden within human society, and struggle with limited resources, personal convictions, and the danger of becoming consumed by the hunt, using rules for desperation, danger, and difficult moral choices.

title: i’m sorry did you say street magic
cover: covers/ttrpg/i’m sorry did you say street magic.jpg
synopsis: A GMless city-building story game in which players collaboratively create a magical urban community. Through rounds of play they establish neighbourhoods, visit landmarks, meet residents, hold events, and let the city change in response. Shared roles and conversation make the place itself the central character, accumulating history, relationships, tensions, and wonder.

title: Imagine Queer Worlds
synopsis: A modular worldbuilding game for examining how fictional societies understand bodies, biology, gender, expression, relationships, attraction, sex, and sexuality. Prompts gradually increase in complexity and work for different group sizes and experience levels, helping creators move beyond inherited assumptions and build cultures whose queer possibilities shape their environments and inhabitants.

title: Imitation Meat
synopsis: A hidden-identity horror game inspired by The Thing, set among scientists and government agents at Antarctica’s McMurdo Station after contact with an alien organism. Using a standard deck, players stage scenes and resolve tricks while uncertainty grows over who has been perfectly imitated, who can be trusted, and whether fire can contain the threat.

title: ION Heart
synopsis: A solo journaling RPG about a Pilot and their Mech exploring a galaxy rebuilding after war. Using d6 prompts, you create systems, planets, and settlements, undertake self-contained Story Circuits, help communities, face dangers, and record how the partnership between Pilot and machine develops; optional rules support two-player play.

title: Kids on Bikes 2e
synopsis: A collaborative roleplaying game about young people confronting strange mysteries in a small town. Players build the community and their relationships together, assign different dice to character strengths, and may share control of a powerful figure. The second edition expands guidance, options, and tools for creating adventures shaped by friendship, danger, and youthful discovery.

title: Koriko
synopsis: A solo journaling game about a teenage witch spending a year away from home in an unfamiliar city. Tarot cards, dice, prompts, and a physical stack of dice guide seasonal chapters about making friends, finding work, developing magic, and gaining confidence, creating a gentle coming-of-age story inspired by magical everyday life.

title: Lancer
synopsis: A science-fiction roleplaying game combining narrative play about pilots with detailed tactical battles between customisable mechs. In a far-future setting shaped by Union and competing powers, characters take missions, build relationships, earn licences, and assemble machines from modular frames, weapons, and systems for grid-based combat with meaningful strategic choices.

title: Lasers and Feelings
synopsis: A one-page science-fiction roleplaying game about the crew of the scout ship Raptor exploring space while their captain recovers from psychic interference. Characters balance a single number between technical precision and emotional intuition, confronting randomly generated threats through quick rolls and improvisation in the spirit of colourful episodic space adventure.

title: Last Oath
synopsis: A solo gamebook about repeated expeditions into a lethal site within a world that has survived several apocalypses. A compact statistic governs health, damage, and inventory while branching rooms, traps, and monsters reward mapping and hard-won knowledge. Death is expected, with each new character benefiting from what earlier attempts revealed.

title: Last Train to Bremen
synopsis: A GMless tragedy for four players portraying musicians who sold their souls for success thirteen years ago. Now they ride a freight train toward the one place they hope the Devil cannot reach. Structured like an unfinished one-act play, the game uses secrets, confrontations, and revelations to drive the doomed quartet toward its final performance.

title: Letters from the Liberty Motel
synopsis: A solo journaling game about the housekeeper of an infinite motel whose guests include beings of every imaginable kind. Each workday sends you through generated rooms to clean what departing residents left behind, answer prompts, and write from changing perspectives. Accumulated tiredness leads to overnight events that gradually bring the strange employment to an end.

title: Liminal Horror
synopsis: A rules-light modern horror RPG in which ordinary people investigate familiar places disrupted by paranatural threats. Clear risks and consequential choices drive play, while encounters with monsters, Stress, and Fallout transform Investigators rather than advancing them through conventional classes or levels; this edition includes character creation, equipment, core rules, combat, and expanded tools.

title: Long Sword
synopsis: A fantasy roleplaying game about sworn knights undertaking quests for their queen, kingdom, faith, people, or personal destiny. Characters are defined through virtues, weapons, backgrounds, oaths, and repertoire, then face tests and lasting fallout on a quest map. It includes guidance for creating missions and an introductory hunt for a unicorn’s grotto.

title: Lord Scurlock
synopsis: A compact fantasy scenario about the estranged children of Lord Scurlock returning to Ilysium after his death. Their inheritance consists largely of debts, a diminished estate, troubling possessions, and creditors already gathering at the manor. Family history and competing claims turn the funeral into a tense situation of obligation, secrets, and desperate choices.

title: Lyrics of Legend
synopsis: A fantasy roleplaying game set in Kkumnala, where gifted performers called Idols channel magic through music, dance, or poetry. They protect communities from demonic bards and other forces that consume souls and drain emotion, making performance both a source of wondrous power and the means to resist a spreading darkness.

title: Maharlika
synopsis: A technomystic science-fantasy mecha game inspired by Filipino history, mythology, and folklore. Pilots serve megacorporate Datus across the Arkipelago, balancing fame and debt while undertaking missions, hacking the spiritual Lambat, confronting Xenobeings, and piloting highly customisable Meka in tactical combat amid a neofeudal galactic order.

title: Masks of the Masks
synopsis: A GMless Powered by the Apocalypse superhero game about how violence reshapes supposed heroes. Presented partly as a comic and partly as rules, it uses masks, pillars, mysteries, and impending doom to question identity, agency, and the genre’s reliance on force, producing stories influenced by morally complicated superhero fiction.

title: Masks Retconned
synopsis: A compact, unofficial reworking of Masks: A New Generation about teenage superheroes learning who they are.
