Players create heroes through origins and shifting labels, then fight villains, support their team, and deal with adults’ expectations. Its deliberately concise rules rely on the group’s knowledge of superhero stories to fill in the wider comic-book world.

title: Megacity Lagos
synopsis: A system-neutral cyberpunk setting framework for a future Lagos shaped by megastructures, dense markets, runaway technology, corporate control, urban decay, and resistance. It provides cultural and setting details, non-player characters, thematic ideas, and plot hooks as a foundation for game masters who want cyberpunk campaigns beyond the genre’s commonly used American cities.

title: Metalepsis
synopsis: A two-player game about living fiction, authorial intent, and a protagonist’s struggle for agency. One participant plays the Author and the other the Protagonist, using cards and structured acts to negotiate or contest control of the story. Alternate rules support solo or three-player play while preserving the conflict between creator and created character.

title: Michigan Dogman
synopsis: A cryptid-hunting roleplaying game for one to three players about seeking proof of the legendary Michigan Dogman. Characters venture from a sceptical tavern into the woods, gather evidence, map their search, and risk encounters with the towering creature and its wild dogs, hoping to return with credibility rather than become part of the legend.

title: Monster Care Squad
synopsis: A pastoral fantasy roleplaying game about healers travelling through Ald-Amura to treat magical creatures afflicted by an unstable force called the False Gold. Players investigate each monster’s condition, gather ingredients, build trust with local communities, and perform collaborative cures, making care, knowledge, and compassion the central forms of heroic action.

title: Monster Truckers
synopsis: An action roleplaying game about classic monsters driving cargo through the post-apocalyptic Worstlands after losing a war with humanity. Ghosts, mummies, vampires, werewolves, and other hard-luck hauliers take dangerous delivery jobs, facing road hazards, mysteries, and violent threats in a low-preparation collision of trucking adventure, wasteland action, and monster comedy.

title: Monsterhearts 2
synopsis: A roleplaying game about teenage monsters navigating desire, identity, cruelty, and volatile relationships. Players embody archetypes such as vampires, witches, and werewolves whose supernatural powers express emotional struggles. String-based influence and dramatic moves drive messy social scenes, while the game treats queerness and uncertain self-discovery as fundamental parts of adolescence.

title: MÖRK BORG
synopsis: A rules-light apocalyptic fantasy roleplaying game set in a dying world of plague, cruelty, and religious dread. Doomed characters seek treasure and temporary survival in lethal dungeons while prophecies steadily count down to the end. Fast d20 rules, random tables, brutal equipment, and an aggressive visual style support bleak, darkly comic play.

title: MÖRK BORG Den of the Degenerate Dirt Diggers
cover: covers/ttrpg/MÖRK BORG Den of the Degenerate Dirt Diggers.jpg
synopsis: A MÖRK BORG adventure location inhabited by filthy, desperate diggers and the horrors surrounding their work. Designed for rapid insertion into a campaign, it provides a grim dungeon environment, inhabitants, threats, treasure, and complications suited to the game’s doomed world, where greed and survival encourage characters to descend despite obvious danger.

title: MÖRK BORG Korg
synopsis: An unofficial digital tool and compact reference for generating and managing MÖRK BORG play. It brings together useful rules, random procedures, characters, equipment, and campaign aids in an accessible format, helping groups create the game’s doomed scum and improvise the bleak encounters, locations, and miseries that await them.

title: MÖRK BORG Last Call
synopsis: A MÖRK BORG scenario built around a final opportunity in a world already approaching its end. It presents a self-contained situation with bleak locations, desperate inhabitants, violent opposition, and the game’s characteristic mix of horror and black humour, ready to use as a short adventure or a grim interruption within a campaign.

title: MÖRK BORG Motstandare
synopsis: A collection of adversaries for MÖRK BORG, expanding the doomed world with additional creatures and hostile figures. Each compact entry supplies game-ready statistics, behaviour, and evocative detail, giving referees a varied set of threats that can be introduced in dungeons, wilderness journeys, settlements, or improvised encounters.

title: MÖRK BORG Punk is Dead
synopsis: A MÖRK BORG-compatible supplement that pushes the game’s apocalyptic attitude through punk culture and its aftermath. It offers additional character material, equipment, encounters, and setting ideas shaped by noise, rebellion, decay, and nihilism, providing groups with another abrasive lens through which to confront the world’s inevitable ending.

title: Mothership
synopsis: A science-fiction horror roleplaying game about vulnerable crews facing isolation, corporate exploitation, hostile environments, and unknowable life in space. Its streamlined rules cover stress, panic, survival, combat, and character creation, supporting tense investigations and expeditions where careful decisions matter and encounters can permanently damage or quickly kill the characters.

title: Mothership Decagone
synopsis: A Mothership adventure structured around a lethal time loop. The crew repeatedly confronts the same catastrophic sequence, using knowledge gained through failure to understand the location, its inhabitants, and the forces trapping them. The scenario turns repetition into investigation while stress, changing choices, and limited opportunities keep each cycle dangerous.

title: Mothership Techromancer
synopsis: A Mothership supplement or scenario centred on dangerous technology that blurs engineering, computation, and the occult. It introduces tools, threats, and situations suited to crews confronting systems that behave like forbidden magic, extending the game’s industrial science-fiction horror through experiments and machinery whose capabilities carry consequences beyond ordinary technical failure.

title: Neon Black
synopsis: A cyberpunk roleplaying game about a found family of radicals struggling against corporate power while trying to protect their community. Built from Forged in the Dark principles, it divides attention between dangerous operations and everyday relationships, making mutual aid, neighbourhood pressures, personal obligations, and resistance central to life in its unequal future.

title: No Prep GM
synopsis: A practical guide to running roleplaying sessions with little or no advance preparation. It reframes the game master’s role around listening, improvising, drawing on familiar stories, and using random tables rather than fixing events in advance. Advice on names, dungeons, likely outcomes, and reusable techniques helps play respond directly to the table.

title: Notorious
synopsis: A solo roleplaying game about a feared bounty hunter pursuing targets across a strange science-fantasy galaxy. Dice rolls and prompts generate planets, factions, encounters, rivals, and complications as the hunter tracks each quarry. The journaled journey builds a compact space-western tale of reputation, violence, solitude, and choices that shape the final confrontation.

title: O Patron Mine
synopsis: A tarot-based solo game about an ordinary person encountering an otherworldly entity and making a pact. Three Major Arcana cards reveal the being, the meeting, and the agreement through guided prompts. It can stand alone as a short reflective story or serve as a prelude that develops another roleplaying character’s desires, fears, and supernatural obligations.

title: Orbital Blues
synopsis: A lo-fi space-western roleplaying game about sad, hard-luck outlaws drifting through a future that has left them behind. Crews take precarious jobs, visit worn-down worlds, and carry emotional troubles called Blues. Its rules make music, memory, friendship, and regret part of adventures inspired by dusty westerns and melancholic science fiction.

title: Otherworldly Flesh
synopsis: A system-neutral exploration setting inside an immense living organism or biological vessel. Its keyed locations transform anatomy into strange environments: fruit, neurons, organs, teeth, acid, parasites, and defensive reactions become rooms, hazards, resources, and discoveries. The result is a compact, visceral crawl where injuring the surrounding body can make the entire place more hostile.

title: Out of the Fold
synopsis: A zero-preparation, GMless magical thriller for two to five players. Magicians attempt to escape the labyrinthine headquarters of the secret society that trained them, building poker hands together to cast spells and drawing cards for obstacles. Flashbacks reveal why they chose to leave and how they came to trust one another.

title: Paint the Town Red
synopsis: A melancholy vampire roleplaying game about depression, partying, love, trauma, vice, and loneliness. Undead characters roam the nightlife of great cities, chasing moments that make them feel alive despite the rot in their souls. Sessions resemble disastrous nights out, where relationships and excess matter more than conventional heroic quests.

title: Parselings
synopsis: A roleplaying game about people bonded with magical fragments of language called Parsecytes. By combining written words, characters can reshape reality, but their powers and identities are entangled with alien influence. The game focuses on collaborative word magic, relationships, self-expression, and conflicts over who controls the meanings that define the world.

title: Pathfinder 2E Core Rulebook
synopsis: The core rules for Pathfinder’s second edition, providing everything needed to create heroes and run detailed fantasy adventures. It presents ancestries, backgrounds, classes, feats, equipment, spells, exploration, encounters, downtime, advancement, monsters, and game-master guidance, built around a structured three-action economy and extensive character customisation.

title: Plane- Teleporter Operator Simulator
synopsis: A solo journaling game about working for AstroFusion as an operator helping travellers teleport between planes. Each turn follows a standard procedure for processing unusual passengers and destinations, with modes ranging from mass transit to a private firm. Optional tower-based chaos introduces malfunctions and a rising crisis index to complicate the job.

title: Prequel
synopsis: A collaborative fantasy game about creating the legendary history that occurs before a final confrontation with a great evil. Players establish a realm, choose heroes with origins and callings, undertake quests, and record how their actions shape the coming battle, producing the shared backstory of a world already poised at its decisive moment.

title: Primadonna
synopsis: A solo game about a once-beloved musician condemned to perform endlessly for the Beast of the End, whose awakening would bring the apocalypse. Using cards and reflective prompts, it explores fame, artistic identity, isolation, helplessness, and the widening divide between what an artist needs and what their audience demands.

title: Psychonaut
synopsis: A Blades in the Dark playbook for an altered-state explorer of the ghost field and collective consciousness. Drugs, alchemy, meditation, and ritual let the character dispense dangerous substances, leave physical limitations behind, and enter other minds, raising the question of whether they are an addicted amateur or a genuine pioneer of psychic experience.

title: Queer Cyberpunks Guide To TTRPGs
synopsis: A zine about bringing queer, anti-establishment perspectives to cyberpunk roleplaying games. It examines how communities, bodies, technology, oppression, care, and rebellion can move the genre beyond familiar corporate dystopias and grizzled stereotypes, offering ideas and prompts for games where punk remains a lived political and creative practice.

title: RAD
synopsis: A post-apocalyptic roleplaying game set in the former Soviet republics after a 1990 American nuclear strike. Survivors cross an irradiated landscape shaped by ruined institutions, mutated dangers, scarce resources, and the remnants of Soviet technology and culture, pursuing bold missions in a setting that mixes wasteland survival with rebellious, darkly comic adventure.

title: Random Realities
synopsis: An oracle zine for solo play, GMless games, preparation, improvisation, worldbuilding, and writing. Every page combines more than sixty results across ten categories, allowing dice, page flips, or PDF links to generate worlds, locations, people, creatures, items, quests, and scenes from densely interconnected fragments rather than separate conventional tables.

title: Rebel Yell
synopsis: A cyberpunk playset for the Paragon system about artists, musicians, poets, and scoundrels resisting conformity in a divided near future. The punks share a manifesto of authenticity, community, and action while challenging authorities that police the Old City, turning performance, solidarity, and public disruption into weapons against oppression.

title: Return of the Lazy Dungeon Master
cover: covers/ttrpg/Return of the Lazy Dungeon Master.jpg
synopsis: A system-flexible guide to helping Gamemasters prepare less while running focused, responsive games. It presents an eight-step preparation process, then expands into advice on running sessions and developing a practical GM mindset; its examples favour fantasy and d20 games, but the techniques do not depend on game-specific mechanics.

title: Rites of Exorcism
synopsis: A collection of extremely compact microgames about demonic possession and attempted exorcism. Each thirty-six-word design uses a handful of six-sided dice and a distinct ritual structure to create questions, visions, prayers, memories, sacrifice, and uncertainty, exploring the struggle among vessel, demon, priest, faith, and despair through sharply constrained play.

title: RPG Design Zine 1
synopsis: A concise how-to zine about tabletop roleplaying design, centred on understanding design as a sequence of purposeful choices. It encourages creators to examine what their rules ask participants to do, why particular structures support the intended experience, and how clarity about those decisions can guide a game from initial idea toward playable form.

title: RPG Design Zine 2
synopsis: A second practical zine about tabletop roleplaying design, focused on tools and techniques learned through making games. Drawing examples from a wide range of independent designs, it encourages experimentation, repeated practice, and deliberate use of structures that shape authority, conversation, uncertainty, and the kinds of stories play can produce.

title: Sanctuary and Sentinel
synopsis: A tragic storytelling game about a place of great power, the Guardians sworn to protect it, and the Threat that will destroy almost all of them. Play establishes the Sanctuary and follows the group’s final defence, knowing that only one Sentinel will remain to remember what was protected and the companions lost in the fight.

title: Session Zero
synopsis: A card-driven character history game that creates an adventurer’s life before their main story begins. Drawing from suits associated with happiness, bonds, character, and sadness, the player answers prompts about formative experiences, relationships, benefits, and harms, producing a rounded past that can stand alone or be carried into another roleplaying campaign.

title: she shall not be raised fey
cover: covers/ttrpg/she shall not be raised fey.jpg
synopsis: A tiny solo story game about exchanging babies with the fey and returning ten years later to witness the consequences. A single die roll reveals whether the child was abandoned, mistreated, hidden, settled, or able to recognise and welcome you, compressing a decade of separation, guilt, and uncertain belonging into one outcome.

title: Shut Up, Kiss Me
synopsis: A light-hearted roleplaying game of romantic melodrama inspired by soap operas and telenovelas. Players create characters driven by conflicting desires, ambitions, families, and relationships, then improvise a densely eventful episode. Simple traits and rolls push scenes between controlled conversation and impulsive feeling while everyone pursues happiness through spectacular emotional complications.

title: SLIMDNGN
synopsis: A compact old-school dungeon-crawling system using six-sided dice for controlled, risky, and desperate actions. Skills, foibles, inventory slots, classic saving throws, resource loss, and escalating narrative dynamite create consequential exploration with minimal rules. Its concise procedures support quick characters, improvised rulings, dangerous combat, and easy adaptation to a referee’s own setting.

title: Slugblaster Slime
synopsis: An expansion for Slugblaster focused on strange biology rather than conventional gear. It adds signatures, equipment, ultraterrestrials, neogens, monsters, runs, and rules for creatures and transformations acquired through symbiosis, mutation, or reckless experimentation, giving teenage hoverboard crews new ways to become entangled with the living ecosystems of the multiverse.

title: Slugblaster Solder
synopsis: A technology-focused expansion for Slugblaster about kids whose inventions, modifications, and bodies blur together. It provides new signatures, gear, loot, salvage, monsters, technobabble, runs, and a featured adversary, supporting crews who treat engineering as identity and solve multiversal problems through improvised devices, upgrades, and dangerously enthusiastic experimentation.

title: Slugblaster Warp
synopsis: A Slugblaster expansion for characters drawn toward the unknowable physics of other dimensions. It adds signatures, gear, warped phenomena, monsters, peelback tables, revelations, runs, and a featured threat, allowing crews to perceive and manipulate spacetime while risking transformative encounters with forces that refuse ordinary scientific explanation.

title: Sly Flourish’s DM Tips
synopsis: A collection of concise advice for running fantasy roleplaying games with less preparation and more flexibility. The tips address session planning, encounter design, improvisation, pacing, non-player characters, locations, and table management, giving Dungeon Masters small practical techniques that can be adopted individually to make games easier to prepare and more responsive to players.

title: So Now You’re a Time Traveller
cover: covers/ttrpg/So Now You’re a Time Traveller.jpg
synopsis: A compact roleplaying game about agents trained to travel through time using their own minds. Because there is only one timeline, witnessed events become obligations that must occur exactly as remembered. Play revolves around incomplete information, causal responsibility, and missions to preserve history without learning facts that make the work impossibly constrained.

title: Songbirds 3E
synopsis: An eldritch fantasy roleplaying game about vulnerable adventurers called Songbirds travelling through a strange, dangerous world. Character gifts and curses, otherworldly pacts, songs, magic, body modifications, exploration, dungeons, spirits, and downtime support journeys shaped by identity and transformation, combining old-school danger with vivid, intimate, and explicitly trans fantasy.

title: Spectral Exterminators
synopsis: A comedic supernatural roleplaying game about jumpsuited professionals eliminating troublesome ghosts. Players build exterminators with traits and talents, roll pools of six-sided dice, spend or earn Brownie Points, identify spirit classifications, and deploy specialised equipment while a Ghoul Master presents hauntings, complications, and opportunities for improvised paranormal problem-solving.

title: Spin the Bottle
synopsis: A horror roleplaying game about former childhood friends reuniting years after several members of their group vanished without explanation. A nostalgic party and familiar bottle game force old memories, suspicions, and relationships back into view, using cards and escalating revelations to uncover what happened and whether the danger has truly returned with them.

title: Spire
synopsis: A fantasy-punk roleplaying game about drow revolutionaries resisting the high elves who rule the towering city of Spire. Characters join a hidden ministry, undertake missions, build influence, and suffer lasting fallout as their rebellion changes districts and relationships. The resistance system emphasises costly victories, political compromise, and the personal consequences of revolutionary action.

title: Spire Magister’s Guide
synopsis: A game-master supplement for Spire offering advice and additional tools for running revolutionary campaigns in the city. It expands approaches to scenario creation, factions, consequences, and the setting’s social pressures, helping the Magister turn player actions into responsive conflicts while maintaining the game’s mixture of fantasy, politics, horror, and escalating fallout.

title: Spire Quickstart
synopsis: An introductory version of Spire that teaches its setting and resistance-system rules through ready-to-play material. It provides pregenerated drow revolutionaries, essential mechanics, guidance for the Magister, and a starting scenario, allowing a group to experience covert rebellion, strange fantasy, and costly consequences without the full core book.

title: Spire Shadow Operations
synopsis: A collection of short scenarios for Spire, each presenting a compact revolutionary operation that can be run alone or inserted into a campaign. The missions span different districts, factions, and forms of resistance, giving the Ministry immediate problems whose political stakes, strange magic, and unintended consequences can reshape the city.

title: Spire Strata
synopsis: A substantial supplement for Spire that turns its attention to the city's richest and poorest districts, contrasting high society with life in the depths. It adds the Inksmith and Shadow Agent classes, setting material, equipment, and advances, alongside ten scenarios divided between the upper and lower reaches of the city.

title: Star Trek Adventures 2E Quickstart
synopsis: An introduction to the second edition of Star Trek Adventures, presenting streamlined rules, pregenerated Starfleet officers, and a ready-to-play mission. It teaches collaborative problem-solving, values, traits, and dramatic task resolution in the Star Trek universe, giving new groups a guided first voyage without requiring the complete core rulebook.

title: Star Trek Adventures Quickstart
synopsis: An introductory package for the first edition of Star Trek Adventures. It supplies essential 2d20 rules, pregenerated members of a Starfleet crew, guidance for the game master, and a complete mission, demonstrating how investigation, diplomacy, scientific expertise, and danger combine in an episode of collaborative Star Trek storytelling.

title: Stars Without Number Revised Free Edition
cover: covers/ttrpg/Stars Without Number Revised Free Edition.jpg
synopsis: A complete science-fiction roleplaying game for sandbox campaigns among the stars. It combines old-school character rules with extensive tools for generating sectors, worlds, factions, adventures, alien ruins, technology, and problems. The free edition supports exploration, trade, intrigue, and combat while helping game masters create an active setting with minimal preparation.

title: Stellar Beacon 1
synopsis: The first issue of a science-fiction roleplaying zine supporting Return to the Stars and broader gaming culture. Its hopepunk theme includes an essay on the genre, a solarpunk scenario, a hard-science-fiction megastructure adventure, encouragement for new game masters, and non-linear prompts for creating optimistic sandbox stories among the stars.

title: Strange Changeling Child
synopsis: A solo game about a child labelled strange because they cannot meet other people’s expectations—and who may genuinely possess fairy magic. Two dice and a single sheet of paper guide struggles, confidantes, meltdowns, concealment, and discovery, exploring whether revealing the character’s true nature brings alienation, acceptance, or a new understanding of belonging.

title: Suites
synopsis: A one-page, setting-neutral roleplaying system that replaces dice with a deck of playing cards. Blackjack-like draws resolve skill contests and combat, while suit-based abilities and ace points let players improve outcomes when fictionally appropriate. Compact character creation, health, damage, and reshuffle rules provide a lightweight chassis for many genres.

title: Superstars- Racing Icons
synopsis: A roleplaying game about racers deciding what will outlast their short careers: trophies, fans, sponsors, or meaningful relationships. Competitive events force choices between safety, friendship, and glory, while players collaboratively build the drama around them. Its flexible premise can portray modern motorsport, motorcycles, mechs, spaceships, or other high-speed spectacles.

title: Tales from the Dungeon 1
synopsis: The first issue of an amateur roleplaying zine, organised around the theme of death. It collects optional rules, non-player characters, locations, grave-related items, backstory tools, lore, hooks, and longer game material, offering varied ways to restore danger, tension, consequence, and mortality to fantasy campaigns.

title: Teeth - False Kingdom
synopsis: A standalone Teeth roleplaying game of occult criminality and monster hunting in a cursed version of eighteenth-century England. Built from Blades in the Dark, it follows desperate characters navigating malign folklore, institutional power, and grotesque threats through operations where investigation, violence, and consequence steadily entangle the crew.

title: The Accessible Design Survival Guide
synopsis: A practical introduction to making tabletop roleplaying publications more accessible. It explains common barriers involving typography, colour, layout, images, digital documents, and assistive technology, offering achievable design choices that improve readability and usability for disabled readers without requiring creators to become specialists in every area of accessibility.

title: The Black Mold of Claus Manor
cover: covers/ttrpg/The Black Mold of Claus Manor.jpg
synopsis: A holiday gothic-horror scenario connected to The Wassailing, steeped in vampires, ghosts, vermin, folklore, and the decay of an old manor. It provides the location, inhabitants, supernatural dangers, and festive grotesquerie needed for an investigation in which seasonal tradition conceals rot, predation, and family secrets.

title: The Cog That Remains
synopsis: A solo game about the chief mechanic responsible for keeping a giant war machine and its pilot alive between missions. Based on The Wretched, it uses scarce supplies, repairs, upgrades, unreliable allies, and mounting failures to explore the unseen labour behind heroic mecha combat and the likelihood of being the only person left afterward.

title: The Complete Guide to Creating Epic Campaigns
cover: covers/ttrpg/The Complete Guide to Creating Epic Campaigns.jpg
synopsis: A guide to designing and sustaining large-scale tabletop roleplaying campaigns. It covers developing central conflicts, villains, factions, locations, character arcs, revelations, and meaningful choices, with methods for organising ideas and pacing events so an ambitious story can remain coherent while still responding to the players’ decisions.

title: The Family Order
synopsis: A tarot-driven storytelling game for three to six players about a family steeped in old and powerful magic. Play follows three generations across three hundred years, recording how relatives, rivals, the wider world, and the family’s magic change before the group decides what future awaits the lineage they have collectively created.

title: The Ground Itself
synopsis: A storytelling game about a place changing across days, years, or centuries. Players define a location, then use cards and prompts to explore moments from its history, shifting perspective between inhabitants and the ground itself. Time can move unpredictably, revealing how memory, conflict, care, and absence accumulate within a shared landscape.

title: The House of Gureaux the Butcher
cover: covers/ttrpg/The House of Gureaux the Butcher.jpg
synopsis: A compact horror location centred on the abandoned home of Gureaux, a butcher whose visits once coincided with villagers disappearing. Rumours, keyed rooms, hidden caves, grisly evidence, and the lingering mystery of his lost daughter turn the house into a system-neutral dungeon where appetite, grief, and human remains are closely entangled.

title: The Lazy DM Workbook
synopsis: A practical workbook of charts, maps, lists, and reference tools for fantasy game masters preparing and improvising adventures. It supports the Lazy Dungeon Master approach with reusable material for names, monuments, dungeons, NPCs, encounters, treasure, traps, and other common needs, reducing the effort required to turn a few strong ideas into playable sessions.

title: The Lazy Dungeon Master
synopsis: A concise guide to preparing fantasy roleplaying sessions by concentrating on the elements most likely to matter at the table. It advocates flexible situations over scripted plots and provides a repeatable method for identifying characters, scenes, secrets, locations, and threats, helping game masters spend less time preparing while remaining ready to improvise.

title: The Praxic Compendium
synopsis: A system-neutral collection of reusable elements for tabletop roleplaying design. Organised by play cycles, genre, authority, focus, resolution, stakes, statistics, bonuses, tracking, and preparation, it adapts mechanisms from many games into modular components that designers can study, combine, rebuild, or use while rapidly prototyping their own systems.

title: The Quiet Year
synopsis: A map-drawing game about a community rebuilding after civilisation’s collapse. Each week, a card introduces a question or event while players add discoveries, projects, shortages, and tensions to a shared map. Discussion is deliberately constrained, making collective priorities and quiet disagreements visible before the Frost Shepherds arrive and bring the year to an abrupt end.

title: The Royal Art Gallery Heist
synopsis: A fantasy heist adventure about stealing the Water Blossom, a painting worth a king’s ransom, from a heavily protected royal gallery. Forged credentials, disguises, guards, magical wards, and a planned jailbreak give characters several layers of security to overcome before a plot twist complicates the promised reward and their escape.

title: The Secret Histories Rulebook
synopsis: The core rules for The Secret Histories roleplaying game, set in the occult world associated with Cultist Simulator and Book of Hours. Players investigate hidden traditions, forbidden knowledge, strange powers, and the consequences of ambition, using a narrative system built for mysteries, personal drives, and encounters with histories concealed beneath ordinary reality.

title: The Secret Histories The Lady Afterwards
cover: covers/ttrpg/The Secret Histories The Lady Afterwards.jpg
synopsis: A complete introductory campaign for The Lady Afterwards, set in 1920s Alexandria within the Secret Histories universe. Players investigate the disappearance of an occult acquaintance through locations, documents, suspects, and esoteric clues, gradually uncovering a dangerous design while learning the game’s rules and the city’s layered historical atmosphere.

title: The Sprawl Corebook
synopsis: A cyberpunk roleplaying game using Powered by the Apocalypse rules for teams of deniable professionals undertaking missions against powerful corporations. Players plan operations, call on contacts and gear, manage corporate attention, and endure consequences between jobs. The campaign develops through the evolving threats and relationships created by the group’s own corporate setting.

title: The Sprawl Downtown Data Heist
synopsis: A ready-to-run mission for The Sprawl involving the theft of valuable information from a secured urban target. It provides objectives, locations, opposition, and complications that demonstrate the game’s legwork and action phases, giving a team of cyberpunk operatives a focused job that can stand alone or begin a wider corporate campaign.

title: The Sprawl Mission Files
synopsis: A collection of missions and game-master resources for The Sprawl. It supplies varied cyberpunk operations with employers, targets, locations, complications, and corporate entanglements, allowing groups to begin quickly or insert new jobs into an existing campaign while showing different ways to structure legwork, action, and consequences.

title: The Sprawl November Metric
synopsis: A scenario or campaign framework for The Sprawl that draws a team of cyberpunk professionals into a corporate operation with escalating consequences. It presents the people, objectives, locations, and hidden interests needed for mission play, using the game’s legwork and action structure to turn incomplete information into pressure and difficult choices.

title: The Sprawl Touched A Darkening Alley
cover: covers/ttrpg/The Sprawl Touched A Darkening Alley.jpg
synopsis: A supplement for Touched, the supernatural expansion of The Sprawl, presenting a dark urban operation where cyberpunk tradecraft collides with uncanny forces. It provides mission material, threats, locations, and complications for professionals whose corporate targets can no longer be understood through technology and violence alone.

title: The Sprawl Touched Prime
synopsis: The principal rules expansion bringing supernatural and occult elements into The Sprawl’s mission-based cyberpunk system. It adds character options, powers, threats, and guidance for combining corporate operations with hidden magic, allowing crews to confront forces that complicate the game’s familiar cycle of legwork, action, attention, and consequence.

title: The Time We Have
synopsis: A two-player zombie tragedy performed on opposite sides of a closed door. Two brothers draw cards and ask questions during the final days before one of them turns, exploring affection, conflict, memory, and farewell as signs of infection worsen. At the end, the surviving brother alone decides whether to open the door.

title: The Ultimate RPG Campfire Card Deck
cover: covers/ttrpg/The Ultimate RPG Campfire Card Deck.jpg
synopsis: A deck of 150 questions designed to spark in-character conversation during tabletop roleplaying sessions. Cards invite party members to reveal backstory, relationships, beliefs, memories, and newly invented details, making them useful during travel, rests, campfires, or other downtime in any genre where players want to understand their characters and companions more deeply.

title: The Ultimate Session Zero Workbook
synopsis: A practical workbook for building a tabletop campaign collaboratively before play begins. It guides the DM through outlining the setting, expectations, and house rules, then provides a step-by-step session zero process with printable questionnaires and character-backstory sheets for gathering ideas and establishing the kind of game the whole group wants.

title: The Walls Will Swallow You
synopsis: A horror roleplaying game or scenario about a place whose architecture is actively hostile to those inside it. Exploration reveals shifting rooms, concealed histories, and mounting supernatural danger as the characters search for escape or understanding, making the building’s transformations and the fear of entrapment central to play.

title: the_bookmarked
synopsis: A post-post-apocalyptic roleplaying game about Tellers who recover lost language and use technomancy to give breath to the breathless. Characters follow paths of discovery, overcome perils, and build knowledge toward climactic encounters, while physical bookmarks and nearby books become part of character creation, progression, scenarios, and the game’s material relationship with words.

title: Thirsty Sword Lesbians
synopsis: A narrative roleplaying game about queer heroes crossing swords, exchanging glances, and fighting injustice in emotionally charged worlds. Playbook moves connect action with desire, vulnerability, and identity, supporting stories that range from swashbuckling romance to revolutionary struggle while giving characters room to discover what they want and who they may become.

title: This Discord Has Ghosts in It
cover: covers/ttrpg/This Discord Has Ghosts in It.jpg
synopsis: A live-action online roleplaying game played inside an empty Discord server. Some participants are investigators exploring text channels as rooms, while others are ghosts who reveal fragments of their deaths through messages and altered spaces. The session becomes a collaborative digital haunting built from improvisation, discovery, and the platform’s own structure.

title: This Old House
synopsis: A reflective game for one to four players about a home and the lives held within it. Using a deck of cards and the physical process of building a house of cards, players create rooms, memories, changes, and inhabitants, allowing the unstable structure to embody how homes accumulate meaning and eventually transform or fall.

title: Tinoli Me Tangere
synopsis: A Filipino historical roleplaying game inspired by José Rizal’s Noli Me Tangere, centred on an elaborate party hosted by Lucrezia Banaag. Guests navigate masks, status, romance, rivalry, food, faith, and colonial society through a sequence of dramatic scenes, with the host’s traditional tinolang manok becoming part of the gathering’s social and emotional stakes.

title: Tournament Arc
synopsis: A GMless, diceless Belonging Outside Belonging game that recreates sports-anime seasons. Players collaboratively define a team, its world, and any imaginable competitive Game, then use playbooks and episode structures for matches, daily life, friendships, rivalries, defeats, and triumphs, whether the activity is football, martial arts, card games, or intergalactic hyper-sport.

title: Transgender Deathmatch Legend II
synopsis: A two-player fighting roleplaying game about a transgender combatant battling across a map of opponents toward a decisive confrontation. Card-based trick taking resolves dramatic matches while relationships, identity, rivalry, and the body give each fight emotional stakes, combining arcade-style progression with a personal story shaped by victory and defeat.

title: Traveller Core Rulebook
synopsis: The core rules for Traveller, a science-fiction roleplaying game about capable people making their way among the stars. It covers lifepath character creation, skills, equipment, starships, travel, trade, encounters, combat, worlds, and campaign preparation, supporting exploration, commerce, politics, military service, and uncertain careers across a broad interstellar setting.

title: Triangle Agency
synopsis: A surreal corporate-horror roleplaying game about employees of the Triangle Agency containing reality-breaking Anomalies. Agents balance missions, office politics, personal lives, and their own anomalous powers while the organisation monitors their performance. The game’s systems divide control among the Agent, their strange ability, and the human identity endangered by the work.

title: Triangle Agency Field Agent Manual
synopsis: The player-facing core book for Triangle Agency, presented as an in-world employee manual for newly recruited field agents. It contains character creation, rules, powers, equipment, procedures, and extensive corporate guidance for investigating Anomalies, navigating bureaucratic expectations, and maintaining a life outside the Agency despite its constant intrusion.

title: Triangle Agency Field Agent Manual 0.3.3.3
synopsis: An earlier playtest edition of the Triangle Agency Field Agent Manual. It introduces the game’s surreal corporate-horror premise, agent creation, anomalous abilities, mission procedures, and competing aspects of character identity, preserving a developmental version of the rules and presentation before the completed release.

title: Triangle Agency One Night at the Shelterwood Inn
cover: covers/ttrpg/Triangle Agency One Night at the Shelterwood Inn.jpg
synopsis: An official Liminal Horror and Triangle Agency crossover adventure offering two approaches to the same disastrous night at an isolated hotel. Ordinary travellers stranded after a crash become caught between corporate interference and a monstrous threat, while Triangle Agency Field Agents arrive on a retrieval mission complicated by missing guests and meddling civilians.

title: Triangle Agency The Vault
synopsis: A Triangle Agency expansion opening the Vault of additional anomalies, assignments, characters, and classified corporate material. It gives General Managers new threats and campaign tools while extending the Agency’s strange bureaucracy, allowing field teams to discover further contradictions, secrets, and reality failures hidden behind the organisation’s official procedures.

title: TROIKA!
synopsis: A surreal science-fantasy roleplaying game about eccentric travellers moving through the infinite spheres. Characters begin with wildly distinctive backgrounds and use compact rules derived from Fighting Fantasy for tests, combat, inventory, and advancement. Its open setting, strange creatures, spells, and adventure material encourage improvisation, wonder, danger, and unexpected connections.

title: Troll Hunter
synopsis: A tabletop roleplaying game about tracking and confronting trolls, with investigation and fieldwork leading toward encounters with dangerous folkloric creatures. Characters identify signs, learn local conditions, prepare suitable tactics, and face beings whose habits and weaknesses vary, making knowledge and planning as important as courage in the final hunt.

title: Tunnel Goons
synopsis: A minimalist adventure roleplaying system built around three broad abilities and a simple two-dice resolution rule. Characters explore dangerous places, carry equipment that directly affects their capabilities, and face consequences without heavy bookkeeping. Its small, adaptable framework makes it easy to customise for different settings or use as the foundation for new games.

title: Vampire the Masquerade
synopsis: A personal and political horror roleplaying game about vampires hiding within modern society. Characters balance hunger, predatory power, human attachments, and obligations to undead factions while maintaining the Masquerade. The game explores moral decline, identity, conspiracy, and the struggle to retain humanity within a culture built on secrecy and exploitation.

title: Vice & Violence
synopsis: A tabletop roleplaying supplement focused on crime, temptation, and brutal conflict. It provides procedures, character material, threats, and situations for stories in which personal appetites and organised violence shape the characters’ choices, supporting campaigns that explore how ambition, coercion, and dangerous pleasures bind people to a hostile world.

title: Wanderhome
synopsis: A pastoral fantasy roleplaying game about travelling animal-folk journeying through the land of Hæth after a long war. With no game master and little emphasis on violence, players share responsibility for places, seasons, and inhabitants while their characters seek belonging, offer care, and decide what home might mean along the road.

title: We Dig Giant Robots
synopsis: A tabletop roleplaying game about a crew operating enormous machines, combining the spectacle of giant robots with the practical relationships required to keep them functioning. Missions, repairs, teamwork, and personal pressures shape play as characters confront threats too large for ordinary people while discovering what their machines and comrades demand of them.

title: WH40K Wrath and Glory
synopsis: A Warhammer 40,000 roleplaying game about diverse Imperial operatives facing war, corruption, aliens, and daemonic threats in the grim darkness of the far future. Its dice-pool rules support characters across several power tiers, from desperate humans to Space Marines, with combat, influence, psychic powers, equipment, and campaign guidance.

title: What’s My Motivation
synopsis: A system-neutral toolkit for creating deeper fictional characters in roleplaying games, novels, and other stories. Prose, prompts, examples, and rollable tables develop backgrounds, inciting incidents, personality traits, values, flaws, and related motivations, helping creators turn broad concepts into individuals whose priorities and imperfections can drive choices, conflict, growth, and change.

title: Wicked Congregation
synopsis: A solo Wretched and Alone operation about an agent sent by a secretive bureau to investigate a town, a strange object, and a dangerous cult. Playing cards reveal the passing days and different aspects of the assignment while isolation and escalating supernatural pressure turn official procedure into a struggle to understand and survive the congregation.

title: Wolves at the Lake
synopsis: A horror worldbuilding roleplaying game about a community beside a lake and the fears gathering around it. Players collaboratively define the setting, resolve actions through merits and flaws, and reveal how people, rumours, landscape, and lupine or supernatural threats shape one another, creating a place whose history deepens as its danger becomes clearer.

title: World Ending Game
synopsis: A structured roleplaying game for giving an established campaign a deliberate final session. Prompts help players revisit important people, places, objects, and unresolved questions, sharing scenes that reveal what the characters leave behind. It turns reflection and closure into play, creating an epilogue shaped by the group’s own history.

title: World of Dungeons
synopsis: A minimalist fantasy roleplaying game that distils old-school dungeon adventure through an early Powered by the Apocalypse framework. Characters are defined by compact abilities, skills, equipment, and magical options, while a single flexible move resolves danger. Its spare rules encourage quick creation, improvisation, exploration, and easy adaptation.

title: World Wide Wrestling
synopsis: A roleplaying game about the spectacle and backstage drama of professional wrestling. Players portray performers competing for audience attention while a creative authority frames shows and feuds. Moves cover matches, promos, interference, and relationships, allowing scripted outcomes and genuine uncertainty to coexist as wrestlers pursue heat, championships, and career-defining moments.

title: Wreck This Deck
synopsis: A solo occult journaling and art game played by physically altering a deck of cards. Each card becomes a record of rituals, entities, protection, and personal discoveries as the player builds a unique magical object. Drawing, writing, tearing, marking, and other transformations make the finished deck both game artefact and story.

title: Xas Irkalla
synopsis: A dark survival-horror roleplaying game set in a hostile, surreal world shaped by suffering and transformation. Characters awaken with little security, confront grotesque environments and beings, and change through the consequences of survival. Its rules emphasise risk, scarcity, psychological pressure, and an oppressive atmosphere rather than heroic power.

title: You Meet In A Tavern, You Die In A Dungeon
cover: covers/ttrpg/You Meet In A Tavern, You Die In A Dungeon.jpg
synopsis: A rules-light, procedurally generated dungeon crawler designed for a chaotic one-shot in which every character is destined to die. Cards and dice create rooms and hazards after the party establishes its ill-fated quest in a tavern, with flexible timing, easy drop-in play, and spotlight deaths that bring the session to its chosen ending.

title: You Will Die In This Place
cover: covers/ttrpg/You Will Die In This Place.jpg
synopsis: An experimental horror roleplaying game presented as the reconstructed, unfinished work of a missing designer. Fragmented notes, rules, sketches, and fiction make the document itself part of the mystery, asking players to engage with a game whose hostile place, uncertain authorship, and repeated promise of death blur the boundary between artefact and story.
